section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an uncontrolled intersection, you should:
options: a:Yield to a vehicle coming from your right and be prepared to stop.,b:Maintain your speed and proceed.,c:Expect other drivers to yield to you.,d:Stop regardless of other traffic.
note: At intersections without signs or signals, yield to the vehicle on your right and be ready to stop to avoid a collision.

question: Lines separating traffic moving in opposite directions are what color?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Black
note: Yellow lines are used to divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: Which lights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Low beam headlights improve your visibility to others and reduce glare in rain or fog; do not use high beams.

question: What is the effect of combining drugs with alcohol on driving risk?
options: a:It increases the chance of causing a crash.,b:It lessens alcohol's effect on driving.,c:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
note: Drugs—including illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter medicines—can impair driving; combined with alcohol they increase crash risk.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights, what action must you take?
options: a:Pull to the curb or road edge and stop until it passes.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,c:Maintain speed and stay in your lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing lights or siren, pull right and stop until it passes.

question: A driver license should be considered a:
options: a:Right.,b:Requirement.,c:Privilege.,d:Guarantee.
note: Driving is a privilege granted by the state and can be suspended or revoked for unsafe or unlawful behavior.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:They are eliminated if you have two outside mirrors.,c:You can check blind spots with rearview mirrors alone.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In a roundabout, what is the correct action for entering traffic?
options: a:Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Yield to entering traffic.,c:Drive clockwise around the central island.
note: Entering motorists must yield to traffic already using the roundabout and proceed counterclockwise around the central island.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but cannot find a gap in traffic, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Maintain your speed and force the other drivers to create a gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.
note: If no gap is available, slow down on the ramp and wait for a safe space to merge; do not stop at the end of the ramp.

question: Why should you be particularly cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,b:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicycle.,c:You are moving faster than the bicycle.
note: When passing bicyclists, be aware they may swerve to avoid hazards and oncoming traffic may not expect you to move out to pass.

question: When traveling to an unfamiliar area, you should:
options: a:Plan your route in advance.,b:Rely only on road signs to find your way.,c:Only have a general idea of where you're going.,d:Depend solely on a passenger to give directions.
note: Plan your trip before you go so you are not distracted or uncertain while driving in unfamiliar areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal shows a red light but a green arrow in the direction you want to go, when may you proceed?
options: a:Only after coming to a complete stop.,b:Only after the light changes to green.,c:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
note: If a green arrow is displayed in your lane, you may proceed in the arrow's direction after yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians still in the intersection.

question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:Improves skills but harms judgment.,b:Harms both driving skills and judgment.,c:Has no effect.,d:Only affects judgment.
note: Alcohol impairs vision, reaction time, coordination, and judgment, reducing your ability to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind uphill, what should you expect?
options: a:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit and passing may be unsafe,b:The truck will always move to the right to let you pass,c:You can safely pass on a hill if the lane is clear,d:The truck must pull over to let faster cars pass
note: Large vehicles often slow on hills; passing on hills with limited visibility is dangerous and often illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle?
options: a:If your lane is next to a solid yellow line — never, this is prohibited,b:On a hill or curve where you can see well ahead,c:By using the shoulder of the highway,d:When the passing lane is clear and the centerline permits passing
note: Do not pass on hills or curves or by using the shoulder; only pass where centerline markings and visibility allow and it's safe.

question: If you must park in an area not normally used for parking, what should you ensure?
options: a:Park five feet from the curb.,b:Park with your reverse lights on.,c:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.
note: Park so your vehicle does not create a hazard and is visible to approaching drivers from all directions.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Simply refuse a drink when offered while already drinking.,c:Drive but call a friend if needed.
note: Deciding ahead not to drive if you plan to drink is the only reliable way to avoid alcohol-related crashes.

question: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane on water, should you immediately apply the brakes?
options: a:True,b:False
note: If you hydroplane, release the accelerator and allow the vehicle to slow; do not immediately apply the brakes.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should allow extra space in front of your vehicle because:
options: a:Station wagons need extra space.,b:Passenger vehicles need more stopping room.,c:Motorcycles can stop quickly and are harder to see.
note: Motorcycles can stop more quickly than cars and are harder to see, so allow extra space to stop safely.

question: May you drive around or under a moving railroad gate?
options: a:No — never drive around or under a lowering or raising gate,b:Yes if the train is far away,c:Yes if you are in a hurry,d:Yes if there is no warning light
note: Do not drive around or under a gate that is moving up or down; wait until lights stop and gates are fully raised.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always come to a full stop.,b:Slow down and yield to traffic and pedestrians.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your left.,d:Speed up to merge.
note: A yield sign means slow down and give the right-of-way to any vehicle or pedestrian already in the roadway you wish to enter.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you use a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane?
options: a:Only if your vehicle has the required minimum number of occupants.,b:If you are driving faster than the flow of traffic.,c:If you are a single occupant and the lane is empty.,d:When you are carrying hazardous materials.
note: HOV lanes are restricted to vehicles meeting the minimum occupancy requirement shown on the signs.

question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:
options: a:Stop to look at the workers.,b:Reduce following distance.,c:Pass carefully and avoid slowing to “rubberneck.”,d:Weave through traffic to get ahead.
note: Do not slow down to stare at incidents; proceed safely and maintain an appropriate following distance and speed through work zones.

question: Which surface is most likely to freeze before the rest of the road?
options: a:A bridge or overpass.,b:An intersection.,c:A downhill slope.,d:A parking lot.
note: Bridges and overpasses are exposed to air on all sides and often freeze earlier and thaw later than regular pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you return to your original lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:As soon as you clear the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.
note: Only move back into your lane when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror to ensure a safe distance.

question: If you are already inside an intersection when the light changes from green to yellow, you should:
options: a:Increase speed to clear the intersection.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection.,c:Continue through and clear the intersection safely.,d:Back up out of the intersection.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, proceed and clear the intersection safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, what must you do regarding oncoming traffic and pedestrians?
options: a:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Expect them to yield to you.,c:Never yield to them.
note: Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before completing a left turn.

question: Why should you increase following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To see around it and better anticipate road conditions ahead.,b:Because they drive slower than other vehicles.,c:To be caught in their slipstream.,d:To reduce fuel consumption.
note: Large vehicles block your view of the road; increasing following distance lets you see around them and react earlier.

question: Where is the safest location for children age 12 and under in a vehicle with airbags?
options: a:The back seat,b:The front passenger seat,c:On the lap of an adult,d:The cargo area
note: Children 12 and under should ride in the back seat where airbags are less likely to cause injury in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when a traffic signal turns green?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible,c:Back up slowly before proceeding,d:Proceed without checking for hazards
note: Yield to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection before proceeding on a green light.

question: True or False: The faster your speed, the longer it takes to stop after reacting to another driver's unexpected move.
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and the time needed to react to unexpected situations.

question: At a railroad crossing, what should you be aware of?
options: a:Vehicles that must stop at all crossings and the possibility of multiple trains.,b:Only trains coming from one direction.,c:That crossings are always clear.
note: Approach crossings with caution; watch for vehicles required to stop (e.g., buses, hazardous material trucks) and for trains from either direction.

question: What's the best way to reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep tires properly maintained,b:Use cruise control in wet conditions,c:Drive faster through standing water,d:Increase tire pressure beyond recommended
note: Proper tire maintenance and reducing speed in wet conditions help prevent hydroplaning; avoid cruise control when roads are wet.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to proceed through a red light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the light turns green.,b:Follow the officer's direction and go through the intersection without stopping.,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.
note: Instructions from a traffic officer override traffic signals and posted signs; follow the officer's directions.

question: Alcohol does which of the following?
options: a:Wakes you up.,b:Puts you to sleep.,c:Slows reflexes and reaction time.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity and reduces the skills needed for safe driving, including reaction time.

question: A diamond-shaped sign typically indicates:
options: a:Road hazard or warning.,b:An interstate route.,c:A school crossing.
note: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and warn drivers of hazards or special conditions ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a single broken white centerline indicate?
options: a:You may cross it to change lanes when safe.,b:You must stay in your lane at all times.,c:You may only change lanes from the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and permit lane changes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding is never dangerous.,c:Only inexperienced drivers are affected by speed.,d:Speed has no effect on crash severity.
note: Both excessive speed and driving significantly below the flow of traffic can create hazards and increase crash risk.

question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:When you have to stop quickly.,b:When passing another car.,c:If you have lost control of your car and need to warn others.
note: Use your horn to alert others to danger, such as when you have lost control and need to warn nearby drivers.

question: How should you drive near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way,b:Take the right-of-way and proceed,c:Continue at the same speed,d:Honk to alert them to your presence
note: Slow and yield to blind pedestrians; be prepared to stop and ensure their safety before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see a 'Merging traffic' sign on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Honk at incoming traffic.,b:Always remain at your present speed.,c:Make room for entering vehicles when possible.
note: On multi-lane roads make room for merging vehicles; if no one is beside you, consider moving over one lane.

question: Why might a large truck swing wide when turning right onto a multilane street?
options: a:Because long vehicles' rear wheels follow a shorter path, requiring extra swing to complete the turn.,b:Because it must stay strictly in the right lane at all times.,c:Because it may complete its turn in either lane equally.
note: Long vehicles often need to swing wide to allow the rear wheels room to clear and complete the turn safely.

question: When driving in fog, should you use your low beam headlights?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams can reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, how should you proceed?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, watch for other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed carefully when safe.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Work hard to steer, slow down, and pull off the road safely,b:Turn off the ignition immediately,c:Honk your horn and keep speed,d:Stop in the travel lane and call for help
note: If power steering stops, steering effort increases; reduce speed, steer carefully to a safe area, and stop.

question: When is it appropriate to turn off your mechanical turn signal?
options: a:Before you begin your turn.,b:In the middle of your turn.,c:After completing your turn.,d:While stopped at a red light.
note: Activate the signal before the turn and turn it off after you have completed the maneuver.

question: At night, when another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights.,b:Use your low beam headlights.,c:Turn off your headlights and use parking lights.
note: Do not use high beams when approaching or following other vehicles at night; switch to low beams to avoid blinding other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which of these actions is prohibited?
options: a:Signal before changing lanes.,b:Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.,c:Cross the centerline in an intersection.,d:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Never attempt to pass or change lanes while inside an intersection; doing so is prohibited and unsafe.

question: If you become tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers.,b:Drink coffee.,c:Open a window.
note: If you feel tired, stop at the first safe opportunity to rest, nap, or change drivers; fatigue reduces reaction time and alertness.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow signal, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain your current speed.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and stop.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns you to be alert and to slow down; proceed only when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are drivers required to use their turn signals when leaving a parking space?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must signal by hand or using directional lights when pulling out of a parking space to inform other road users.

question: In winter, if a road surface seems dry, is it definitely dry?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Roads that appear dry can still be slippery due to black ice, especially on bridges, overpasses, and shaded areas.

question: What are 'No zones' around trucks?
options: a:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close they restrict the truck's maneuverability.,b:Places with several car lengths between vehicles.,c:Spaces that provide sufficient room to travel behind a truck.
note: 'No zones' are truck blind spots or areas where cars are dangerously close and limit the truck driver's ability to maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another car, how can you be sure you have enough space to return to your lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror,b:When the other driver waves you back,c:When you are one vehicle length ahead,d:When you hear the passed car's horn
note: Return to the lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and it's safe.

question: When approaching a pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, or other assistive device, drivers should yield the right-of-way:
options: a:True,b:False,c:Yield only if they are in a marked crosswalk.,d:Stop and physically assist the pedestrian.
note: A person with a disability using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or other device has the same pedestrian rights and must be yielded to.

question: Should you avoid driving beside large vehicles for long periods?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots on both sides; avoid driving alongside them for long periods and either drop back or move ahead.

question: When is using your horn inappropriate?
options: a:Near blind pedestrians,b:When visibility ahead is limited,c:If you might hit another vehicle,d:To warn someone of immediate danger
note: Avoid using your horn around blind pedestrians as it may cause confusion or danger; yield and proceed only when safe.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
options: a:Speed up to cross before a train arrives.,b:Look and listen for trains and be ready to stop.,c:Drive around lowered gates.,d:Ignore warning signs if no train is visible.
note: Slow down, look, and listen for trains; be prepared to stop and obey gates and warning lights.

question: When is it legal to drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never — do not go around or under a lowered gate,b:If the warning lights are not flashing,c:When you can see clearly in both directions,d:If no train is visible
note: You must never drive around or under a lowered crossing gate; wait until it is fully raised and the crossing is clear.

question: How should you check your vehicle's blind spots?
options: a:Turn your head and glance over your shoulder to view blind spots.,b:Rely exclusively on your side mirrors.,c:Check only your rearview mirror.,d:Use only the vehicle's backup camera to check blind spots.
note: Blind spots are areas your mirrors won’t show. Turn your head and glance over your shoulder to verify those areas before changing lanes.

question: On gravel or dirt roads, how does traction compare to pavement and what should you do?
options: a:You have less traction than on pavement, so slow down and allow greater stopping distance,b:You have better traction so you can drive faster,c:Visibility is always better,d:You should tailgate to stay stable
note: Loose surfaces reduce traction and increase stopping distance and skidding risk; reduce speed and increase following distance.

question: Which of the following happens after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:Your judgement of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You are less alert.,d:All of the above
note: Alcohol reduces reaction time, impairs vision, distorts judgement of speed and distance, and decreases alertness.

question: A person using a white cane or guide dog should be treated as:
options: a:A deaf pedestrian.,b:A blind pedestrian.,c:An inattentive pedestrian.,d:A pedestrian in a crosswalk only.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian who is blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Signal and pull into the slow lane.,b:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.,c:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.
note: Get your vehicle off the travel lanes if possible and turn on emergency flashers so other drivers can see you.

question: What characterizes defensive driving?
options: a:Keeping your eyes moving to detect possible hazards,b:Focusing only on the car directly ahead,c:Maintaining one car length of space at all times,d:Driving with only one hand on the wheel
note: Defensive driving involves scanning the road and surroundings continuously to anticipate and avoid hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds,b:Slow speeds,c:Driving at night.
note: Higher speeds lengthen stopping distance and increase collision impact and severity.

question: Which traffic signal condition requires you to stop, yield to cross traffic/pedestrians, then proceed when clear?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A steady green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A steady yellow light.
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: stop completely, yield, and then proceed when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper way to make a right turn?
options: a:Signal, slow, and enter the lane nearest the right curb before turning.,b:Signal, accelerate, and use the lane closest to the centerline.,c:Approach in right lane then move toward the center before turning.
note: Approach the corner in the rightmost lane, signal, slow down, and stay close to the right curb when turning right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Come to a full stop, then proceed when safe.,b:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,c:Treat it as a flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing red light means stop, yield the right-of-way, and proceed only when safe—like a stop sign.

question: At a light rail crossing, what must you do?
options: a:Look both ways before crossing tracks.,b:Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.,c:Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
note: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Look both ways and obey all signs and signals when crossing rail tracks.

question: On the road, bicycles are considered:
options: a:Vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.,b:Hazards that must always yield to cars.,c:Not subject to the rules of the road.
note: Bicycles are vehicles and bicyclists must follow the same rules as motor vehicle drivers.

question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:Are passing a bicyclist.,b:Are traveling through an intersection.,c:See a child who is about to run into the street.
note: Use your horn to warn others of immediate danger, for example if a child appears about to run into the road.

question: Are signs used in construction work zones typically orange?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Most temporary work zone signs are orange and often diamond-shaped to warn drivers of construction activity.

question: On slick or slippery roads, how should you take turns?
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Accelerate through the turn.,c:Change lanes quickly before turning.,d:Brake hard in the middle of the turn.
note: Reduce speed and negotiate turns more slowly on slick surfaces to maintain control.

question: A solid white edge line that angles toward the left indicates:
options: a:The road will narrow or the shoulder ends ahead.,b:An upcoming intersection.,c:A required left turn ahead.,d:A pedestrian crossing.
note: An edge line slanting toward the center shows the road or shoulder is narrowing ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.,b:Often, even at controlled intersections.,c:Never; it confuses other drivers.,d:Only at uncontrolled intersections.
note: Yield your right-of-way whenever doing so will help prevent a crash; do not assume other drivers will always yield to you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to an emergency vehicle using lights or a siren?
options: a:When you hear a siren or see flashing red or blue lights.,b:Only if other drivers yield first.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle that is using its siren or flashing lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, who should yield?
options: a:You should yield to drivers already on the public road.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:You may force your way into traffic.
note: Vehicles entering from driveways or private roads must yield to traffic already on the public roadway.

question: Which device or activity increases a driver's crash risk due to distraction?
options: a:Cell phone use.,b:Listening to the radio.,c:Operating the CD player.
note: Using a cell phone (even hands-free) or other audio devices can greatly distract drivers and raise crash risk.

question: What is the correct method to check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Look over the shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter and check mirrors.,b:Only turn and look over your right shoulder regardless of direction.,c:Trust that outside mirrors eliminate blind spots.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check all mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear.

question: What should you do when driving on potentially slippery roads?
options: a:Reduce your following distance.,b:Reduce speed and avoid sudden speed or direction changes.,c:Use cruise control to hold a steady speed.
note: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden speed or steering changes; do not use cruise control.

question: A safe way to drive through a curve is to:
options: a:Slow down before entering and accelerate gradually as you exit.,b:Maintain the same speed through the curve.,c:Speed up before entering and slow in the curve.,d:Brake hard in the middle of the curve.
note: Reduce speed prior to entering the curve and then increase speed gradually after you exit to maintain control.

question: Under what circumstances may you text while driving in Rhode Island?
options: a:If you are using a voice-to-text feature.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If you can text without looking at your phone.
note: Texting while driving is prohibited in Rhode Island because it is a major distraction to the driver.

question: At a railroad crossing that has only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights, what should you do?
options: a:Only continue once cleared to do so by a flagger, if applicable.,b:Turn your radio down to hear if there may be an approaching train.,c:Approach all tracks with extreme caution and cross only when you know that there is no train coming.
note: Always approach such crossings carefully and only proceed when you are sure no trains are approaching from either direction.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is headed toward you in your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.,b:Blow your horn, steer left, and brake.,c:Blow your horn, steer right, and accelerate.
note: Honk to attract attention, attempt to escape to the right, and brake firmly; avoid swerving left into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right,b:The larger vehicle has the right-of-way,c:The vehicle on the right yields to the left,d:The faster vehicle goes first
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit indicates:
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:The recommended speed for bad weather.,c:A suggested pace for pedestrians.,d:The exact safe speed for any condition.
note: Speed limits set the maximum (or minimum) lawful speed under normal conditions; adjust speed lower for hazards or poor conditions.

question: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you and creates a hazard, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Swerve into the lane next to you.
note: Remove your foot from the accelerator to create space between you and the vehicle ahead without sudden braking or swerving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn, you should:
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels straight while waiting.,b:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,c:Flash your headlights to get other drivers to let you through.,d:Back up slightly to get out of the intersection.
note: Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left; if struck from behind you won't be pushed into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to merge back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,b:After about three seconds.,c:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: You may move back into the right lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make the turn quickly from your lane of travel.,b:Stop and back up.,c:Continue driving to the next exit or other safe location to turn around.
note: Do not back up or make sudden lane changes; continue to the next exit where you can safely turn around.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Only when you see a stop sign,b:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop and at red lights,c:Only when a red light is steady,d:Only when a traffic signal is flashing red
note: You must stop when directed by a police officer and at steady or flashing red lights; always obey officers directing traffic.

question: Which of the following is true about emergency vehicles?
options: a:They have the right-of-way when using sirens and/or flashing lights.,b:They may follow each other but never use loudspeakers.,c:They do not require other drivers to yield.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens and follow any instructions delivered via loudspeaker.

question: When it begins to rain while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Speed up to reach shelter.,b:Drive at the posted speed limit.,c:Slow down and increase following distance.,d:Turn off headlights to save battery.
note: Reduce speed, increase following distance, and turn on headlights to improve visibility in rain.

question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving typically:
options: a:Make no driving errors.,b:Have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicle.,c:Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
note: Eating or drinking while driving distracts hands and eyes from driving tasks, increasing the chance of errors and lane drift.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling 55 mph need to stop?
options: a:About 400 feet.,b:About 50 feet.,c:About 125 feet.
note: Large, fully loaded tractor-trailers can need nearly 400 feet to stop when traveling at 55 mph.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low beam headlights (and fog lights if available) in fog; high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you at a safe distance?
options: a:Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b:Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.,c:Maintaining a steady speed.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling turns, lane changes, and deceleration in advance helps drivers behind you maintain a safe following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do your brake lights communicate to drivers behind you?
options: a:Are slowing down or stopping.,b:Are making a turn.,c:Have your emergency brake on.
note: Brake lights warn other drivers that you are slowing or stopping; they must be working whenever you drive on the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, which action is important?
options: a:Signal, check blind spot, and ensure the lane is clear.,b:Signal and immediately move over.,c:Check one mirror and change lanes quickly.,d:Flip your hazard lights on.
note: Before changing lanes, signal your intent, check mirrors and blind spots, and confirm the target lane is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is the correct procedure for changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, glance over your shoulder, then change lanes.,b:Rely solely on mirrors without signaling.,c:Signal only as you move into the next lane.
note: Signal, check all mirrors, and look over your shoulder to verify the adjacent lane is clear before changing lanes.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: On two-lane roads, drivers in both directions must stop for a school bus that is stopped with flashing red lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally (not in a crosswalk), what must you do?
options: a:Should honk your horn at them.,b:Do not have to stop for them.,c:Must stop for them.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians even if they are not in a crosswalk; stop to avoid hitting them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must give the right-of-way to a pedestrian who is:
options: a:In a marked crosswalk.,b:Crossing any street.,c:In any crosswalk or intersection.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks; be prepared to yield to people crossing streets.

question: An advisory speed sign for a curve should be considered:
options: a:An advisory speed indicating a recommended safe speed under ideal conditions.,b:A speed that may be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy weather.,c:A legally enforceable maximum speed in all conditions.
note: Advisory speeds indicate the recommended safe speed under normal conditions; you must slow down further in poor weather or road conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may not perform a turnabout in which of the following situations?
options: a:Where it would interfere with surrounding traffic.,b:On hills, curves, or where visibility is limited.,c:Where double yellow lines or signs prohibit turnabouts.,d:All of the above.
note: Do not attempt turnabouts where they are prohibited, unsafe, or where visibility or traffic conditions would make them dangerous.

question: Construction zone signs are typically what shape and color?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with an orange background and black markings.,b:Round with yellow and black coloring.,c:Square with red and white coloring.,d:Blue with white lettering.
note: Work zone signs use orange backgrounds with black symbols or letters to warn drivers of temporary conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing by driving on the right shoulder of the road is allowed:
options: a:Only when the car in front of you is turning.,b:Only when there are no pedestrians nearby.,c:Never allowed to pass by driving on the shoulder.
note: You may not leave the paved roadway or drive on the shoulder to pass; pass only where it is legal and safe.

question: A lap belt should be adjusted so it:
options: a:Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,b:Is loose for comfort.,c:Is tucked beneath the seat.,d:Rests across your neck.
note: Lap belts should sit low across the hips and lower abdomen and be worn snugly to provide proper protection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb required?
options: a:Yes — it is required by law and a good habit,b:Only necessary if other traffic is present,c:Only required during the maneuver itself,d:Not required at all
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes; signaling is required by law and a safe driving habit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required but there is no marked stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:At the nearest point where you have a clear view of approaching traffic without entering the intersection,b:You are not required to stop,c:In the center of the intersection to get a better view,d:Only at least 200 feet from the intersection
note: Stop at the nearest point to the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersection.

question: What colors are used for signs that show distances to highway exits?
options: a:Green with white letters,b:Yellow with black letters,c:Red with white letters
note: Destination and guide signs on highways are green with white letters or symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, if you and the driver on your left arrive at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:The driver on your right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,c:Whoever signals to turn first.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

question: From top to bottom, what is the proper order of the standard vertical traffic signal lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Green, red, yellow.
note: Standard vertical traffic signals are arranged from top to bottom as red, then yellow, then green.

question: What can happen when alcohol and another drug are combined?
options: a:The effects of both may be increased,b:There is no interaction,c:The effects of both are always reduced,d:Only prescription drugs interact with alcohol
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can amplify impairing effects, making driving much more dangerous.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: A pentagonal sign marks a school zone or crossing; be alert for children and prepare to stop.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicates:
options: a:Traffic next to the broken line may pass when safe; traffic next to the solid line may not.,b:Passing is not permitted for either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,d:The road is one-way.
note: When a broken yellow line is adjacent to a solid yellow line, only traffic on the broken-line side may legally pass.

question: When you approach a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and proceed when clear.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Treat it like a steady yellow light.,d:Stop only if other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop completely, check both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may pass another vehicle if the dividing line is which type?
options: a:Broken white line.,b:Solid yellow line.,c:Double solid yellow.
note: Broken white lines separate same-direction lanes and allow lane changes and passing when safe.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility, you should drive more slowly and turn on:
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Emergency flashers.,c:Headlights.,d:Interior dome light.
note: Use headlights when visibility is poor so others can see you; increase speed only when safe or pull off if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at the next corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles also turning left.,b:Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a 'Walk' signal.,c:All approaching vehicles.
note: When turning left you must yield to other approaching vehicles, pedestrians, and bicyclists who have the right-of-way.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train, when must you stop?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted.,b:If a crossing gate is lowered.,c:If the crossing lights are flashing.,d:Any of the above.
note: Stop when warning devices are active, a stop sign is posted, a gate is down, a flagger signals, or if a train is visible or too close to safely cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Yes.,b:No.,c:If there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Two solid yellow lines indicate that neither lane may cross the lines to pass except to turn into a driveway or entrance; passing over double yellow lines is not allowed.

question: What should you do when you hear a fire engine siren behind you?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Drive with your flashers on.,c:Slow down until it passes you.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or siren, move to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: When driving on wet pavement, what should you remember?
options: a:Pavement is especially slippery just after rain begins,b:Wet roads never cause hydroplaning,c:You can stop normally without extra distance,d:Never reduce speed after rain starts
note: Roads are especially slick just after rain begins due to oil and dirt mixing with water; slow down and increase stopping distance.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Sharply away from the curb.,b:Towards the curb.,c:Slightly to the right.,d:Straight ahead.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheels sharply away from the curb so the vehicle rolls into the curb rather than into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in a left-turn lane and there is oncoming traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Signal about 100 feet before the turn and keep wheels straight until you begin the turn.,b:Turn your front wheels to the left before starting.,c:Move to the left of the center lane.,d:Signal only after you reach the intersection.
note: Signal in advance and keep your wheels straight until it is safe to begin the left turn to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind.

question: Round traffic signs typically warn of:
options: a:No passing zones.,b:Upcoming railroad crossings.,c:School zones.,d:Stop requirements ahead.
note: Round signs are used to warn drivers of railroad crossings ahead and to exercise caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn should you signal to inform other drivers of your intention?
options: a:At least 100 feet before turning.,b:About 50 feet before turning.,c:20 feet before turning.,d:10 feet before turning.
note: Activate your turn signal at least 100 feet before the turn to properly alert other drivers of your intended maneuver.

question: When driving in fog, which lights are best to use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Low beams and fog lights (if available) provide better visibility in foggy conditions than high beams.

question: Which factor does NOT affect vehicle stopping distance?
options: a:Your reaction time,b:The time of day,c:The condition of your brakes,d:The vehicle's speed
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, brakes, tires, road conditions, vehicle weight, and speed — not on the time of day.

question: Who benefits most from wearing seat belts?
options: a:Only the driver,b:All occupants of the vehicle,c:Front seat passengers only,d:Passengers on long trips
note: Seat belts are most effective when every occupant in the vehicle wears one — they protect all passengers in a crash.

question: Blue roadway signs primarily provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services (like rest areas or hospitals).,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Distance/mileage information.
note: Blue signs are service signs indicating motorist services such as food, gas, or hospitals.

question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:As they would a stop sign — come to a complete stop then proceed when safe,b:Continue through if no crossing traffic is present,c:Slow down but do not stop,d:Only stop if an officer is present
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop and proceeding only when safe, similar to a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrian waves.,b:Only if the pedestrian is paying attention.,c:At all times.,d:Only when the pedestrian has a hand signal.
note: You must stop and yield the right-of-way to any pedestrian in a crosswalk; only proceed when your lane is clear and it is safe to do so.

question: How can you prevent hydroplaning in rain?
options: a:Reduce speed when driving in the rain and maintain good tire tread and pressure.,b:Keep tires underinflated to increase contact area.,c:Use cruise control to maintain speed.
note: Prevent hydroplaning by slowing in wet conditions and keeping tires properly inflated with good tread.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If there is no marked crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:
options: a:Make eye contact and then pass.,b:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.,c:Slow down and pass closely.,d:Proceed as normal.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even when there is no marked crosswalk; stop if needed to let them cross.

question: If you are part of a line of vehicles crossing a railroad track, is it safe to stop on the track for a short time?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Never stop on railroad tracks. Ensure there is room on the far side before you cross so you will not be stopped on the tracks.

question: What does a steady yellow traffic light indicate?
options: a:Slow down and prepare to stop — the light will soon be red,b:Go through the intersection at normal speed,c:Yield to all traffic only,d:Accelerate to clear the intersection
note: A steady yellow warns the light is about to turn red; slow and prepare to stop if you can do so safely.

question: Which behavior helps prevent crashes by making your actions predictable to others?
options: a:Drive only on side streets and back roads.,b:Ignore other drivers on the road.,c:Communicate with other road users.
note: Signal your intentions and use warnings like horns or lights when appropriate to reduce unexpected actions and crashes.

question: True or False: You do not have to stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights if it is on a private road.
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only if the bus is on a public road.,d:Only when no children are present.
note: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm extended, drivers must stop whether the bus is on public or private roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At an intersection with a stop sign.,b:Where there is a red light.,c:When a traffic officer orders you to stop.,d:All of the above
note: You must stop at stop signs, at red signals, and whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
options: a:Eight feet,b:15 feet,c:20 feet
note: Do not park within eight feet of a fire hydrant to ensure emergency access and visibility.

question: If you intend to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Keep driving at a steady speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop for you.,c:Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move over.
note: Deal with one hazard at a time: let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the pedestrian when it is safe.

question: How should you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Use only the inside rearview mirror,b:Turn your head to check blind spots in addition to mirrors,c:Only use the outside mirrors,d:Rely solely on your turn signal
note: Always look over your shoulder to check blind spots before every lane change in addition to using mirrors.

question: Which action helps prevent you from becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Relax and concentrate on driving.,b:Tailgate the driver in front of you.,c:Drive above the posted speed limit.
note: Keep calm, focus on the task of driving, and allow extra travel time to avoid aggressive behaviors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror,b:When the passed vehicle signals you,c:As soon as you pass its front bumper,d:Only after signaling twice
note: Return to your lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and it is safe.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what is the correct response?
options: a:Stay off the brakes and steer in the direction you want to go,b:Brake abruptly to stop the skid,c:Turn the wheel sharply opposite the skid,d:Shift into neutral immediately
note: Do not brake during a skid; steer where you want the vehicle to go and regain control before braking gently.

question: If you stop along the road at night, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Turn off all your lights.,b:Use your parking lights only.,c:Use low beam headlights and emergency flashers.
note: If you stop at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on so other road users can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you merge onto an interstate highway?
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into traffic,b:Always stop before entering the highway,c:Merge across two lanes at once,d:Enter at any speed without signaling
note: Find a safe gap in traffic and merge smoothly at an appropriate speed; don't stop on the ramp unless necessary.

question: Is it allowed to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:When the train has passed.,c:When the flashing lights have stopped.
note: Never go around a lowered crossing gate; signals and gates indicate an approaching train.

question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog to improve visibility?
options: a:Yes — high beams always improve vision,b:No — use low beams or fog lights,c:Yes — but only on rural roads,d:No — turn headlights off and use parking lights
note: In fog or mist, use low beam headlights or fog lights; high beams reflect back and decrease visibility.

question: What is the best way to avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Know what is happening around your vehicle.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.
note: Constantly observe the area around your vehicle—front, sides, and rear—to spot problems early and react safely.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A rectangular red sign.,b:A circular green sign.,c:A reflective orange triangle.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle and indicates the vehicle is traveling 25 mph or slower.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A double solid yellow line separates opposite-direction traffic and indicates that passing is not permitted.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has high beams on at night and it's hard to see, what should you do?
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Look straight ahead, keeping your lane.,c:Stop until the vehicle passes.
note: Avoid looking directly at bright headlights; glance to the right edge of your lane and watch from peripheral vision.

question: A curb painted red indicates:
options: a:Loading zone.,b:Reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c:No parking, standing, or stopping.
note: You may not stop, stand, or park at a red-painted curb.

question: When is it acceptable to cross a dashed (broken) white line?
options: a:Only during daylight.,b:When you need to pass and it is safe.,c:At any time.,d:Only in emergencies.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may cross them to change lanes or pass if it is safe to do so.

question: Regulatory signs primarily:
options: a:Indicate what a driver must or must not do.,b:Are placed only where there is present danger.,c:Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.,d:Provide information about nearby services.
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers the laws and regulations for a particular area (speed limits, no turns, etc.) and must be obeyed.

question: If a HAWK (pedestrian) signal shows a solid red, what must drivers do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A solid red indication on a pedestrian-activated HAWK requires drivers to stop until the signal allows movement.

question: When you see or hear an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes.,b:Slow down and continue driving.,c:Motion for it to pass you.
note: Immediately pull to the right and stop for approaching emergency vehicles using lights or sirens; if in an intersection, clear it first.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.,b:Accelerate quickly.,c:Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
note: After a bus stop, look for children walking near the roadway and proceed with caution; they may dart into traffic.

question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead on the road?
options: a:Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
note: Search the road ahead and to the sides to identify and respond to hazards early; do not simply stare at the center of the roadway.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.,b:Blind spots are eliminated by one outside mirror.,c:You can check blind spots using only the rearview mirror.
note: Even with mirrors, blind spots remain; large trucks' blind spots are much larger than those of cars.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a flashing red traffic light, you must:
options: a:Treat it as a stop sign and stop.,b:Keep going if no other vehicles are visible.,c:Only yield to vehicles from the left.,d:Wait until it turns green automatically.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop; proceed only when the way is clear.

question: At an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow traffic light, you must:
options: a:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,b:Wait for the green light before proceeding.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: Flashing yellow means reduce speed, be alert, and proceed with caution when safe.

question: True or False: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride their bikes.
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only if cyclists use a headlight and reflectors.,d:It is equally safe day or night.
note: Cycling at night is riskier because visibility is reduced; both cyclists and motorists must be extra cautious after dark.

question: At a crosswalk, drivers must:
options: a:Yield to pedestrians in or entering the crosswalk.,b:Expect pedestrians to yield to vehicles.,c:Only yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks.,d:Require construction workers to yield.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks; drivers must yield and stop for them when required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:If the traffic on that street moves to the left.,b:If traffic on that street moves to the right.,c:Only if you speed up before turning.
note: You may turn left onto a one-way street only when traffic on that street moves left and no sign prohibits it.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:Motorcycles can stop quickly, so you need extra distance.,b:They do not follow the same traffic rules.,c:They always brake more slowly than cars.
note: Motorcycles can stop faster than many vehicles, so following too closely can lead to rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to which vehicles?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles going straight ahead.,b:No one.,c:Only overtaking cars.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming vehicles proceeding straight through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:After signaling for three seconds.,c:When the other driver signals you to return.
note: Only return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your inside rearview mirror.

question: After a train passes and stops at a crossing where you were waiting, you should:
options: a:Proceed immediately once the train has passed.,b:Look for a second train and wait until flashing signals stop and gates are raised.,c:Drive around lowered gates if they are blocking traffic.,d:Honk to signal other drivers to go.
note: Even after a train passes, another train may be approaching on another track; wait until all warning devices stop and gates are fully raised.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or attempting to pass another vehicle, you should:
options: a:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,b:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,c:All of the above.,d:Speed up to pass without checking.
note: Always check your mirrors and blind spots and signal your intention before changing lanes or passing another vehicle.

question: To be able to turn quickly and safely, your hands should be placed:
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:Next to each other on the top of the wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the wheel.,d:With your hands crossed.
note: Placing both hands on opposite sides of the wheel gives you better control for quick, safe steering inputs.

question: What is true about driving through roadwork zones?
options: a:You must 'Slow for the Cone Zone' and follow lower speeds and directions,b:Fines are always the same as normal traffic,c:Slow down only if you think workers are present,d:You can drive normally if workers are not visible
note: Drive carefully, slow down, and follow posted instructions in work zones; fines and penalties can be higher for violations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit while driving on the interstate, what is the correct action?
options: a:Continue driving and use the next exit.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,c:Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
note: Do not make sudden turns or U-turns on the interstate; proceed to the next exit and re-route from there.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only at marked crosswalks,b:At all times,c:Only when a crossing guard is present,d:Only if they are in a crosswalk
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way at all times.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you glance?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road,b:At the vehicle's headlights,c:Toward the left side of the road,d:Directly at the lights
note: Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded and maintain enough visibility to stay on course.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians:
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,b:Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.,c:Only on the same side of the road as the driver.,d:Only when the driver has a green light.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if they appear to be careless or are crossing against a signal.

question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,b:Keep a steady pace.,c:Stay in the driver's blind spot.
note: Do not remain in another vehicle’s blind spot; move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.

question: If you see a deep puddle in your path, what should you do?
options: a:Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.,b:Avoid the puddle if possible.,c:Maintain the posted speed to make it through the water.
note: To prevent skids and loss of control on slippery surfaces, avoid deep puddles when possible; the safest surface is dry and solid.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you required to signal every time you pull away from a curb?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Use your turn signal whenever pulling away from the curb to notify other road users of your intent.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:
options: a:Yield to any car already within the roundabout.,b:Yield to any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists.,c:Both of the above.
note: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout as well as to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing the entry.

question: When passing a bicyclist safely, you should:
options: a:Give them as much space as possible and slow down.,b:Honk to alert them to move right.,c:Use the bike lane to pass quickly.,d:Speed past in the same lane.
note: When overtaking a bicyclist, slow down and provide as much lateral space as possible; cyclists are more vulnerable than motor vehicle occupants.

question: When roads are slippery, how should you adjust following distance?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Use alternate routes only.
note: On slippery roads give extra space between vehicles because stopping distances increase.

question: When a pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane is crossing, what must you do?
options: a:You must tell them where to cross the street.,b:You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.,c:You must always yield the right-of-way.
note: Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way; stop and wait until they are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When your slow speed disrupts normal traffic flow.,b:When driving in a work zone at night.,c:Only on rural roads.,d:When following large trucks.
note: You must not drive so slowly that you interfere with the normal flow of traffic; doing so can result in a citation.

question: Which of the following are common effects of alcohol on driving?
options: a:Loss of concentration, poor coordination, and slower judgment.,b:Improved coordination and faster reaction time.,c:No effect after one drink.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not working due to a power outage, how should you proceed?
options: a:Use hand signals to indicate your intentions to other drivers.,b:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and proceed with caution.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed through the intersection without stopping.
note: When signals are out, drivers should yield as at a four-way stop: come to a full stop, then proceed in turn when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,b:Only a recommended driving speed.,c:The exact speed needed to avoid a ticket in all situations.
note: A speed limit indicates the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; drivers should slow when conditions are poor.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what does that mean for turning drivers?
options: a:May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.,b:May no longer turn and must proceed straight.,c:You still have the right-of-way to turn.
note: When the green arrow ends, drivers may still turn in that direction but must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: What does a reduced speed sign stating '35 mph' tell you?
options: a:The new 35 mph limit begins at that sign.,b:You can wait until the next speed sign to slow down.,c:You have plenty of time to reduce speed after the sign.
note: A posted reduced speed sign indicates the new speed limit starts at the sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer is directing traffic at an intersection with functioning signals, you should:
options: a:Follow the traffic signals.,b:Follow the officer's directions.,c:Honk to get the officer's attention.,d:Ignore both and proceed carefully.
note: An officer's instructions at an intersection take precedence over traffic signals and signs; follow the officer's directions.

question: Why must you use extra caution when approaching a pedestrian using a white cane?
options: a:He or she is a police officer.,b:He or she is deaf.,c:He or she is blind.
note: A white cane or guide dog indicates the pedestrian is blind or visually impaired; yield and take extra care to avoid harm.

question: If another driver cuts you off, how should you respond?
options: a:Flash your lights and speed up.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Pull alongside and yell.,d:Brake abruptly to warn them.
note: Avoid road rage by not taking it personally: let it go and maintain safe driving behavior.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you be especially sure to do?
options: a:Flash your headlights as you pass.,b:Sound your horn as you pass.,c:Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
note: Ensure there is ample distance and time to pass safely by judging the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles.

question: What qualifies as a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that takes attention away from driving.,b:Anything that makes you focus more on driving.,c:Only electronic devices.,d:Only passengers under 16.
note: A distraction is any activity or condition that diverts your attention from driving and increases crash risk.

question: What is a common effect of continuous hard braking on ice and snow?
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.,c:Keeps the brakes from freezing.
note: Continuous hard braking on icy or snowy roads can lock wheels and cause a loss of steering control.

question: When making an emergency roadside stop, must you set the parking brake?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Set your parking brake and turn on emergency flashers during an emergency roadside stop to alert other drivers.

question: Signs that alert drivers to potentially hazardous conditions ahead are called:
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.,d:Guide signs.
note: Warning signs are designed to advise drivers of upcoming hazards or changes in roadway conditions and should be obeyed.

question: How can you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?
options: a:Briefly glance toward the right side of the road,b:Focus on the centerline directly ahead,c:Flash your high beams at them,d:Look directly at the lights to adjust
note: Look briefly toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights, then resume scanning ahead.

question: If your vehicle lacks ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Firmly pump the brakes,b:Hold the brake pedal down continuously,c:Tilt the steering wheel while braking,d:Lightly tap the brakes repeatedly
note: For vehicles without ABS, pumping the brakes helps stop quickly while allowing you to steer.

question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:At your side mirror.,b:Over your left shoulder.,c:Over your right shoulder.
note: Glance over your left shoulder to visually check the blind spot in the direction you intend to move.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, what is the safest way to pass a bicyclist traveling in the same direction?
options: a:Do not pass the bicyclist until you come to a traffic signal or stop sign.,b:Continue driving straight; it is the bicyclist’s responsibility to get out of your way.,c:Slow down and wait until there is no oncoming traffic, then pass while leaving enough space.
note: Pass bicyclists as you would other vehicles: wait for a safe gap and allow sufficient clearance, at least 3 feet where possible.

question: Why must you be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They are more difficult to see than cars.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.,c:They rarely use their headlights.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to hide in a vehicle's blind spot; it can be hard to judge their speed and distance.

question: What should you do when approaching an accident scene?
options: a:Keep your attention on driving and keep moving unless you are involved or help has not arrived.,b:Stop to watch and block traffic.,c:Drive to the scene to get a closer look.
note: Do not stop at crash scenes unless you are involved or emergency help hasn't arrived; keep moving and remain alert.

question: Is parking in the access aisles beside handicap stalls permitted?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Parking in handicap access aisles is prohibited; these spaces are reserved for mobility devices and vehicle access.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach an intersection, what is your best action?
options: a:Be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so,b:Speed up to beat the red light,c:Brake abruptly without regard to following traffic,d:Turn quickly into a side street
note: A steady yellow means the light will soon turn red; slow and prepare to stop if you can do so safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Passing in marked no-passing zones or over railroad crossings.,b:Passing when you have clear visibility.,c:Passing when the vehicle ahead signals left.,d:Passing in multi-lane highways where allowed.
note: It is illegal to pass in marked no-passing zones, on railroad crossings, at street intersections, or where signs prohibit passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Using the inside rearview mirror.,b:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using your side mirror.
note: Even with properly adjusted mirrors there are blind spots; turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check them before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: If vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the driver on your right and proceed when it is safe.

question: The effect of sleep deprivation on driving ability is comparable to the effect of:
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Amphetamines.,c:Anger.,d:Caffeine.
note: Being awake for long periods impairs driving similarly to alcohol; for example, 24 hours awake can affect you like a BAC of around 0.10%

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When can you proceed through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop and confirming it is safe to proceed.,b:After slowing down to check for cross traffic only.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
note: If a stop sign has no marked line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and go when safe.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what is the first thing you must do?
options: a:Stop.,b:Call the police.,c:Determine if anyone is injured.
note: If you are involved in a crash, stop your vehicle; then check for injuries, call emergency services if needed, and exchange information.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn not permitted?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.
note: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where your view of approaching traffic is limited.

question: How would you describe distracted driving?
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Extremely risky behavior.,c:Nothing to be concerned about.
note: Distracted driving is a dangerous behavior that greatly increases the likelihood of crashes and injuries.

question: On a freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on city streets?
options: a:In order to see potential hazards early.,b:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.
note: On the freeway you should search farther ahead to spot changing traffic conditions, merging vehicles, and hazards early.

question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow signal instructs drivers to slow down and proceed with caution.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is in your area, what is your responsibility?
options: a:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,b:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.,c:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the side and allowing them a clear path when it is safe to do so.

question: If you have oncoming traffic on your left and parked cars on your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Steer a middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,b:Steer closer to the parked vehicles than to oncoming traffic.,c:Move into the oncoming traffic lane.,d:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles than to the parked vehicles.
note: When faced with oncoming traffic one side and parked cars on the other, steer a middle course to maximize clearance from both hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to drive off the paved roadway to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:If there are two or more lanes in your direction.
note: You may not leave the paved or main-traveled portion of the roadway to pass another vehicle.

question: What does an orange and red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle indicate?
options: a:The vehicle is slow-moving.,b:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:Shoulder work ahead.
note: An orange-red triangle identifies a slow-moving vehicle such as farm equipment or maintenance vehicles.

question: A solid yellow arrow displayed at a turn lane means:
options: a:You may proceed through the turn immediately.,b:The protected turn signal is ending; prepare to stop.,c:You are required to stop in the turn lane.,d:The arrow has no special meaning.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that the protective turning period is ending and you should prepare to stop or yield to oncoming traffic.
