section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a four-way stop, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: At a four-way stop you yield to the driver who arrived before you; proceed when it is your turn.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When directed by a flagger,b:Only if gates are present,c:Only if no other traffic is present,d:Only during daylight
note: Stop when directed by a flagger or stop sign; also stop when flashing red signals and gates are operating.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing red lights and the stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the bus resumes motion and signals are retracted.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if you don't see any children.,c:Proceed at normal speed but watch for children.,d:Pass slowly if the opposite lane is clear.
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights and the stop arm is out, all drivers must stop until the bus retracts the arm and resumes motion.

question: Which method will sober you up after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Drinking caffeine,b:Eating high-fat foods,c:Time — letting your body metabolize the alcohol,d:Taking a cold shower
note: The only way to lower BAC and sober up is to allow time for the body to eliminate alcohol.

question: How should lane changes be executed?
options: a:Gradually and carefully.,b:Quickly and often.,c:Without signaling.,d:Only when traffic is clear.
note: Change lanes smoothly and cautiously, signaling and checking mirrors and blind spots before moving.

question: Before backing out of a driveway with children nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Exit the vehicle and walk to the rear to ensure the way is clear,b:Rev your engine to alert children,c:Sound the horn only once,d:Back up slowly while watching mirrors
note: Get out and check behind your vehicle before backing to ensure children or obstacles are clear; do not rely solely on mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing at an intersection without signals?
options: a:The driver must yield.,b:Whoever started moving last.,c:Whoever is walking slower.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections without traffic lights.

question: When parking uphill beside a curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Keep the rear tires against the curb.,b:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,c:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should complete the turn into:
options: a:The lane nearest to your previous lane.,b:The right lane.,c:The farthest lane from your approach.,d:Any lane available regardless of markings.
note: Turn into the lane closest to your approach to maintain lane discipline and avoid conflicts.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do on a two-lane road?
options: a:Stop immediately and let the vehicle pass.,b:Drive as far toward the right side of the road as is safe and stop.,c:Proceed slowly and permit the vehicle to pass.
note: On two-lane or undivided roads, move to the right as far as safe and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Where pavement markings and signs permit and it is safe to do so.,b:Within an intersection if there is no oncoming traffic.,c:On a curve if visibility is clear.,d:Over a railroad crossing.
note: Pass only where signs and lane markings allow it and when you have sufficient space and clear visibility to complete the maneuver safely.

question: Why is extra space needed in front of a large truck?
options: a:Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.,b:The truck driver needs room to stop the vehicle.,c:Other drivers when they want to slow down.
note: Large trucks take longer to stop than cars; leaving extra space in front gives the truck driver room to brake safely.

question: If you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle while on a divided multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, move over to provide a clear path, and stop if necessary,b:Ignore it if there are other lanes for it to use,c:Speed up to avoid delaying it,d:Stop immediately in your lane regardless of traffic
note: Slow down and move to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle; stop only where safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection at the posted speed and the signal turns yellow, you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.,b:Speed up to cross before the light turns red.,c:Slow down and proceed through without caution.,d:Continue at the same speed and enter the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns the light is about to turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is the posted maximum speed limit always the fastest you can safely drive in an area?
options: a:False,b:True
note: The posted maximum is the legal limit under ideal conditions; you must drive slower when conditions (weather, visibility, traffic) require it.

question: Which of the following can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Changing a radio station or CD.,b:Talking or texting on a cellular phone.,c:Eating, drinking, or smoking.,d:All of the above.
note: Distracted driving can result from any activity that takes attention from driving, including phone use, eating, or adjusting controls.

question: Are roads especially slippery when it first starts to rain?
options: a:True — oil and dirt on the road make it especially slippery at first,b:False — rain always improves traction,c:True — only on highways,d:False — only with heavy rain
note: Roads can be extra slippery when rain first begins due to oil and debris mixing with water; reduce speed accordingly.

question: How should you react to a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard; slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.

question: The space needed to cross traffic safely depends on:
options: a:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic.,b:The color of your vehicle.,c:Whether your turn signal is on.,d:The time of day only.
note: Safe crossing requires sufficient space considering road surface, weather, and the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and slash through a black symbol means:
options: a:The action pictured is forbidden.,b:Drivers must come to a full stop.,c:Some drivers must yield.,d:Drivers may proceed with caution.
note: A red circle with a slash over a symbol indicates the depicted action is prohibited by law.

question: How should you treat a motorcycle sharing the road?
options: a:Allow the motorcycle a full lane.,b:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.,c:Allow the motorcycle only half a lane.
note: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles and must be given a complete lane to operate safely.

question: If other drivers around you are reacting angrily, how should you respond?
options: a:Distance yourself from the situation,b:Make eye contact and argue back,c:Use hand gestures to calm them,d:Speed up to get away quickly
note: Avoid eye contact and gestures; slow down, move over, or otherwise distance yourself to reduce risk of escalation.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign indicate?
options: a:Alerts drivers to school zones.,b:Warns of existing or possible hazards.,c:Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs that indicate potential hazards ahead and are usually yellow or orange.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Passing permitted when no oncoming traffic.,c:Prepare to stop for pedestrian crossing.,d:Two-way left-turn lane ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing from either direction except for permitted left turns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection but can't see because opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before turning.,b:Accelerate when the first lane clears.,c:Proceed when an oncoming driver waves you across.
note: Do not begin a left turn until you can see that all lanes you must cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

question: When another driver is tailgating you, you should:
options: a:Create extra space in front of your vehicle and avoid sudden braking.,b:Speed up to get away from the tailgater.,c:Continue at the same distance as before.,d:Slow down abruptly to teach them a lesson.
note: If someone is tailgating, increase the space ahead of you and avoid abrupt braking; move over when safe to allow them to pass.

question: In dense fog, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams cause glare and reduce visibility.

question: On a slippery road, your following distance should be:
options: a:Farther from the vehicle ahead than normal.,b:No different than normal.,c:Closer than normal.,d:Exactly two seconds regardless of conditions.
note: Slippery surfaces increase stopping distance. Increase your following distance to give more time to stop safely.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding the posted speed limit and driving too fast for conditions.,b:Scanning the environment and staying focused.,c:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,d:Driving well below the posted speed limit.
note: Driving faster than posted limits or too fast for conditions are frequent contributing factors in crashes; always drive at a safe speed.

question: Which of the following is a dangerous habit when driving in work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle.,b:Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment.,c:Both of the above.,d:Ignoring only temporary lane markers.
note: In work zones, following too closely and failing to watch for workers or equipment are both hazardous and increase crash risk.

question: Which type of traffic sign requires drivers to obey the instruction indicated?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs impose legal requirements; failure to obey them can result in penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway from a ramp, you should:
options: a:Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.,b:Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.,c:Check for cars, accelerate to match the flow of traffic, and merge when it is safe.
note: Use the acceleration lane to gain speed and merge smoothly with the flow of interstate traffic; do not stop on the ramp.

question: When a school bus is using its flashing red lights, may drivers pass it?
options: a:True,b:False
note: When a school bus is stopped with flashing red lights, drivers must stop until the lights are turned off, unless separated by a median as specified by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a good general rule to remember about passing other vehicles?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.,b:Try to get to the front of any slow-moving traffic so that you can see better.,c:Pass on the right whenever possible.
note: Passing increases crash risk; stay with the flow, obey speed limits, and pass only when necessary and safe.

question: If another driver is passing your car, how should you respond?
options: a:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing,b:Pull off the road to let them pass,c:Accelerate to prevent the pass,d:Signal them when to pass
note: Maintain steady speed or adjust slightly to help the other driver pass safely and return to the lane.

question: What occurs when you drink alcohol while taking medicines?
options: a:The combination may multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine,b:The medicine cancels out the alcohol,c:Alcohol has no impact on prescription drugs,d:Alcohol will cure side effects of medicines
note: Alcohol combined with medications can amplify impairing effects and increase danger when driving.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent:
options: a:Won't have any effect on your driving.,b:Won't put other drivers at risk.,c:Will double your chances of having an accident.
note: Even small increases in BAC substantially raise the risk of being involved in a fatal crash.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Try to fight it.,b:Take a break.,c:Take some caffeine pills.
note: If you feel drowsy, stop at the first safe rest area to nap, stretch, or change drivers; caffeine is not a substitute for rest.

question: You must stop before crossing railroad tracks when which of the following is true?
options: a:There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.,b:The railroad crossing is located in a city or town with frequent train traffic.,c:You are transporting two or more young children in a passenger vehicle.
note: Always ensure you can completely clear the tracks before entering; stop if you cannot fully cross or if warning devices indicate a train.

question: Which of the following is true about passing a motorcycle?
options: a:A motorcycle with two people on it is more balanced than a motorcycle with just one rider.,b:It is okay for drivers of other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.,c:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane; change lanes completely to pass safely and give them space.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.,b:Large trucks and buses require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.,c:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
note: Heavy vehicles need more distance to stop; sudden stops in front of them increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal while parking next to a curb?
options: a:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to the curb.
note: Signal both when approaching a curb to park and when leaving the curb to inform other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic.,b:Pedestrians who are already in the intersection.,c:Other drivers who are already in the intersection.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians or bicyclists who have the right-of-way.

question: If someone has been drinking, what will help them overcome the influence of alcohol?
options: a:Hot coffee,b:Fresh air,c:Only the passage of time will overcome the effects of alcohol.
note: Nothing speeds the removal of alcohol from the body; only time will reduce blood alcohol concentration.

question: If a bicyclist disobeys traffic laws, what can happen?
options: a:Is in the right because bicyclists don’t have to obey traffic laws.,b:Can be ticketed.,c:Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers; they can be cited for violations of traffic laws.

question: If heavy smoke covers the roadway ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce speed, move as far to the right as possible, and stop off the roadway,b:Turn on four-way flashers and continue at the same speed,c:Turn on high beams and continue,d:Stop in the travel lane and wait for smoke to clear
note: If the road ahead is covered with heavy smoke, slow down, pull as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway until safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in a residential area?
options: a:25 mph.,b:35 mph.,c:45 mph.
note: When driving in a residential area the maximum speed limit is 25 miles per hour unless a different limit is posted.

question: What is the only proven way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drinking coffee.,b:Exercising.,c:Allowing time for your body to metabolize the alcohol.,d:Taking a cold shower.
note: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol; coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not lower BAC.

question: Why is night driving more difficult?
options: a:Distance and speed of other vehicles are harder to judge due to reduced visibility,b:Speed limits are higher at night,c:There are more cars on the road at night,d:Headlights improve depth perception
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to judge distance and speed; headlights only illuminate a limited distance.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:
options: a:Are always cautious because they know the risks.,b:Often do not have sufficient control of their bodies or vehicles.,c:Drive better because they are more careful.,d:Are unaffected at low doses.
note: Alcohol impairs control of both body and vehicle operation; even small amounts can reduce driving ability.

question: What do signs with orange backgrounds indicate?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Construction and maintenance warning signs.,c:General warning signs.
note: Orange is used for construction and maintenance warning signs to alert drivers that work is being done on or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you make room for vehicles entering the freeway?
options: a:Merge into a different lane if possible.,b:Maintain your lane and speed regardless.,c:Speed up to block them.,d:Stop in the lane to let them in.
note: If safe, merge over to create space for entering vehicles; otherwise, adjust your speed to allow them to merge smoothly.

question: When may you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the yellow line next to your side is broken.,b:When the opposite yellow line is broken.,c:If the car ahead moves to the right to let you pass.
note: A broken yellow line adjacent to your lane indicates you may pass if it is safe to do so.

question: Under normal conditions, what minimum following distance should you maintain?
options: a:Three seconds,b:Two seconds,c:One second,d:Four seconds
note: Keep a minimum three-second following distance under normal conditions; increase it when conditions worsen.

question: Why must drivers be especially alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They are smaller and more difficult to see.,b:They follow different traffic laws.,c:They always have the right-of-way.,d:They are always faster than cars.
note: Smaller road users can be harder to spot and are more vulnerable; drivers should be extra attentive to avoid collisions.

question: When approaching a person crossing with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the person is safely away from your path,b:Sound your horn and pass slowly,c:Drive around them if there is room,d:Wait until they wave you on
note: Yield and stop for pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog until they are well clear of your path.

question: Before turning the ignition on, what should you do regarding seat belts?
options: a:Buckle your seat belt and ensure all passengers are buckled,b:Buckle only backseat passengers,c:Buckle only adult passengers,d:No seatbelt checks are necessary until after starting
note: Make a routine of buckling your own seat belt and ensuring all passengers are belted before starting the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should always signal when which of the following?
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.,c:All of the above.
note: Use your turn signals whenever you change lanes, pull into traffic from a curb, or perform other lateral movements to alert others.

question: Because motorcycles and mopeds are harder to see, what should drivers do?
options: a:Make constant visual checks and be alert.,b:Share a lane with a motorcycle.,c:Slow down only when you see a motorcycle ahead.
note: Motorcycles are easily hidden in blind spots; drivers must make frequent visual checks to spot them.

question: If your turn signals stop working, what should you use to indicate turns?
options: a:Hand signals.,b:Your headlights.,c:Your horn.
note: Use standard hand signals to indicate turns if your vehicle's turn signals are inoperative.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the pavement while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.,b:Reduce speed gently, then steer back onto the pavement when safe.,c:Slam on your brakes and stop.
note: Continue with wheels off the pavement, slow gradually by gentle braking, and when at a safe speed steer back onto the road; do not jerk the wheel.

question: How is defensive driving defined?
options: a:Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.,b:Driving aggressively to avoid hazards.,c:Risking more to save time.
note: Defensive driving means adjusting your driving to road, weather, personal condition, and others to avoid crashes.

question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?
options: a:Yes — they increase visibility,b:No — use low beams or fog lights,c:Only on highways,d:Only if other cars use high beams
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: How close to a railroad track are you allowed to park?
options: a:You may not park within 50 feet of the railroad crossing.,b:You may park within 25 feet.,c:You may park within 40 feet.
note: Parking is prohibited within 50 feet of a railroad crossing to avoid obstructing visibility and safety.

question: When taking any medicine, what should you do regarding driving?
options: a:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about its effects before driving,b:Assume over-the-counter drugs are always safe,c:Drive only during daylight hours,d:Have a companion follow you home at all times
note: Check label warnings and consult a health professional about how medications may affect your driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you start across an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red?
options: a:Under any circumstances.,b:Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.,c:Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely without blocking traffic when the light changes.

question: If you arrive at your car upset or angry from work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Play the radio loudly so you won’t think about it.,b:Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.,c:Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin your drive home.
note: Allow yourself time to calm down before driving; emotional distractions impair judgment and increase crash risk.

question: At a HAWK pedestrian crossing, what does a flashing yellow signal instruct drivers to do?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Proceed with no caution.
note: A flashing yellow HAWK signal warns drivers to slow and prepare to stop for pedestrians.

question: If you are upset or emotionally distracted, how should you handle driving?
options: a:Take time to calm down before starting to drive.,b:Drive as usual; emotions do not affect driving.,c:Drive faster to get to your destination sooner.
note: Emotional states like anger or sadness can impair driving; calm down and focus before driving.

question: What do work zone signs indicate about driving conditions?
options: a:It is summer.,b:You must immediately stop and back up.,c:Less than ideal driving conditions are present.
note: Work zone signs (orange) warn that construction or maintenance is occurring and that you should use extra caution.

question: What should you do first when visibility decreases while driving?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers.,c:Turn on your headlights.,d:Pull over to the side of the road.
note: When visibility is reduced, your initial action should be to slow down to give yourself more time to react and maintain control.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:
options: a:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Because of large blind spots, avoid driving alongside large commercial vehicles for long periods; move ahead or drop back so the driver can see you.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, what should you do?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed.,b:Speed up.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: Reduce speed on wet, snowy, or icy roads because your tires have less traction and stopping distances increase.

question: What is the only effective way to eliminate alcohol from your body?
options: a:Take a cold shower.,b:Wait.,c:Drink strong coffee.
note: Only the passage of time removes alcohol from the body; nothing speeds up the process.

question: True or false: Your speed does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you begin braking.
options: a:True.,b:False.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance; as speed rises, the distance needed to stop grows significantly.

question: Which action can reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allowing extra travel time.,b:Tailgating to keep traffic moving.,c:Using hand gestures at slow drivers.,d:Speeding to get ahead.
note: Planning ahead and allowing extra travel time reduces stress and the temptation to engage in aggressive driving behaviors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you must:
options: a:Must yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.,b:Must yield to vehicles only on your right.,c:Should slow down but never stop.
note: Approach yield signs prepared to stop and give right-of-way to any traffic close enough to be a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permitted to cross double solid yellow centerlines?
options: a:To enter a driveway or make a left turn.,b:To pass a slow-moving truck.,c:To pass another car.,d:To avoid debris in your lane.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing and lane changes. You may cross them to make a left turn into or out of a driveway or entrance where permitted.

question: Which lights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams can reflect back and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you complete the turn?
options: a:Into the left lane of the one-way street.,b:Into the center of the street.,c:Into the right lane of the one-way street.,d:Into any lane as long as it is safe.
note: Complete the left turn into the lane nearest to the lane you came from — typically the leftmost lane of the one-way street.

question: You should always use your turn signal when:
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,d:Passing another vehicle on a highway.
note: Use your turn signal to communicate your intentions whenever changing lanes, entering traffic, or leaving parking areas.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest practice when vehicles are approaching?
options: a:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,b:Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles when in a crosswalk.,c:Enter a crosswalk at any time because drivers must stop.,d:Wait until a walk signal or until traffic has stopped.
note: Do not step into the roadway when vehicles are approaching; wait until it is safe even if you would have the right-of-way.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be a danger, you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross the tracks at your own risk.
note: Look and listen for trains before crossing tracks. If a train is approaching and is a danger, you must not cross; wait until it has passed.

question: Which restraint combination is most effective in a crash?
options: a:Only a lap belt.,b:An airbag alone.,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,d:Seat cushion only.
note: A lap/shoulder belt used with an airbag provides the most protection in frontal crashes.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of the road means:
options: a:Passing is permitted when it is safe from either direction.,b:Passing is prohibited in both directions.,c:Only buses may pass.,d:Pedestrian crossing ahead.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate opposing traffic and allow passing when it is safe to do so.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct steering response?
options: a:Overcorrect.,b:Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,c:Turn your steering wheel into traffic.
note: If your vehicle skids, remain calm and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: Which statement best describes defensive drivers' thinking?
options: a:They know other drivers will do the right thing.,b:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate likely mistakes by others and are prepared to respond safely.

question: What should you do before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:Listen and look both ways; proceed only if it is safe.,b:Rely only on signals and cross when they permit.,c:Cross quickly if you see a train in the distance.,d:Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
note: Always look and listen for trains from both directions and obey crossing signals; never proceed until you are sure it is safe.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicates what?
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Slow down.,d:Two-way traffic ahead.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane means passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: What does the term 'No zone' refer to?
options: a:A term used to describe blind spots around a truck or bus.,b:A special speed zone.,c:A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.
note: Trucks and buses have large blind spots on each side, in the rear, and in front; these are called the 'No zone.'

question: Which of the following affects how quickly a person absorbs alcohol?
options: a:Intelligence,b:Weight,c:Height
note: A person's weight, biological sex, stomach contents, and number of drinks affect alcohol absorption and blood alcohol concentration.

question: An inattentive driver is someone who:
options: a:Stares at objects off the roadway or daydreams while driving.,b:Only watches the vehicle directly ahead of them.,c:Maintains eye contact during a conversation with a passenger while driving.,d:Regularly checks mirrors and scans the road.
note: Distraction or daydreaming reduces the driver's ability to see and respond to hazards; remain attentive and continually scan the road.

question: If a child appears about to run into the street, what should you do immediately?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn,b:Start preparing to slow down without warning,c:Flash headlights only,d:Drive around the child
note: If a child or pedestrian is about to enter the roadway, a sharp horn blast may be necessary to warn them and prevent a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection and are not in the correct lane to turn, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,b:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,c:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.
note: Do not make last-minute lane changes. If you are not in the proper lane to turn, continue to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning right on a green light, you must:
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic as required.,b:Maintain your normal speed without looking.,c:Always come to a complete stop even if clear.,d:Only yield to vehicles, not pedestrians.
note: Unless prohibited by sign, turning on green is permitted but you must yield to pedestrians and other road users lawfully in the intersection.

question: When a traffic signal displays a steady green arrow, what does it allow?
options: a:Turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection,b:Stop and wait for a green circle,c:Proceed without yielding to pedestrians,d:Turn only if the main green light is also on
note: A steady green arrow allows the indicated turn after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: When a green arrow is displayed, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.,b:Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.,c:Wait four seconds before proceeding.
note: A green arrow means you may turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: If you see pedestrians near the road, you should:
options: a:Speed up to clear the area.,b:Sound your horn and continue.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.,d:Drive into the opposing lane to avoid them.
note: When pedestrians are near the roadway, reduce speed and be prepared to stop for their safety.

question: When an emergency vehicle is using lights or sirens and approaches you, you must immediately:
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Pull to the right and slow down without stopping.,c:Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.,d:Maintain your speed and keep driving.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with warnings, you must drive to the right and stop to clear a path.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of:
options: a:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.,b:Being late for an appointment.,c:Missing an exit.
note: Fatigue impairs judgment and reaction time and can cause drivers to fall asleep at the wheel, increasing crash risk.

question: When must you pull over and allow an emergency vehicle to pass?
options: a:Regardless of the emergency vehicle's direction, pull over to the right and stop,b:Only if it is following you,c:Only if it is coming from the opposite direction,d:Only if lights and siren are both present
note: You must pull to the right edge and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or siren regardless of its approach direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles to your right and left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on your right has the right-of-way,b:The vehicle on your left has the right-of-way,c:The largest vehicle goes first,d:You should always wait until there are no vehicles
note: When multiple vehicles arrive together at an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the driver's left arm extended downward indicate?
options: a:The driver intends to stop.,b:The driver plans to turn left.,c:The driver plans to turn right.
note: A left arm extended down is the conventional hand signal indicating an intent to stop or slow.

question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Retaliate by tailgating them.
note: If threatened by an aggressive driver, do not engage; give them space, do not make eye contact, and let them pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To avoid being affected by traffic merging from on-ramps to your right on an interstate, what is the best action?
options: a:Change lanes to the left.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down.
note: When safe and traffic permits, move out of the right lane to allow merging vehicles to enter more easily.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver may pass on a two-lane roadway marked with a single solid yellow line on their side of the centerline:
options: a:False,b:True
note: If your side of the centerline is a solid yellow, passing is not allowed from your lane; only pass where a broken line is next to you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, at what speed should you be driving?
options: a:Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.,c:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
note: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic to merge safely without disrupting flow.

question: True or False: Drivers are not required to yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk.
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only at marked crosswalks.,d:Only if the pedestrian is jaywalking.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks (marked or unmarked) and must stop for them when appropriate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on an interstate, what sequence should you follow?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.,b:Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.,c:You should always use cruise control.
note: Before changing lanes or passing on an interstate, signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency.

question: When should you use your horn?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:To express frustration at slow drivers.,c:To get a pedestrian to hurry.,d:To greet a friend on the road.
note: Use the horn sparingly and only to alert others to immediate danger or to avoid collisions.

question: What shape is a stop sign?
options: a:Square.,b:Octagon.,c:Circle.,d:Rectangle.
note: Stop signs are uniquely octagonal; all eight-sided signs require drivers to come to a full stop before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to turn left on a green light but heavy oncoming traffic is present. What should you do?
options: a:Wait in the intersection if necessary and safe to prepare to turn,b:Turn immediately and force your way through,c:Use the next intersection only,d:Back up to let oncoming traffic pass
note: You may enter the intersection on a green to wait for a safe gap to complete a left turn if it is safe and no other vehicle ahead plans to turn left.

question: When used on public roads, bicycles are considered:
options: a:Vehicles.,b:Hazards.,c:Dangerous.
note: Bicycles operating on roadways are legally considered vehicles and follow the same rules.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is correct?
options: a:It is illegal to go around lowered gates at crossings,b:You never have to stop for a flagger at a crossing,c:All crossings have flashing lights and gates,d:You may go around gates if no train is visible
note: You must stop when directed by flaggers, stop signs, flashing lights, or lowered gates; it is illegal to go around lowered gates.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Only illegal drugs impair driving,b:Even over-the-counter medications can impair driving,c:All prescription drugs are always safe,d:Herbal supplements have no effect
note: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs, including cold and allergy medicines, can impair driving and may make driving unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Use your signal.,b:Turn the wheel immediately.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Activate your turn signal several seconds before making the turn to warn other road users.

question: If a vehicle with high beams approaches and doesn't dim them, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the center of the road,b:Toward the right side of the road,c:Directly at the headlights,d:At the oncoming vehicle's wheels
note: Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded and keep enough view to maintain course until the vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you are required to yield to merge into traffic but cannot do so safely, yield also means:
options: a:False,b:True
note: If you cannot safely merge when required to yield, you must stop and wait for a safe gap.

question: Which foot should you use for braking and accelerating?
options: a:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.,b:Use your left foot to brake.,c:Always brake abruptly to stop quickly.
note: Use your right foot for both accelerator and brake to maintain control and avoid sudden, harsh stops.

question: Which statement about small children riding in vehicles is correct?
options: a:They may be safely held by a strong adult.,b:They will be safe if standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,c:They must be properly fastened into an appropriate child restraint.
note: Children must be secured in appropriate child safety seats or restraints; adults cannot reliably hold a child in a crash.

question: If the centerline consists of one solid yellow and one broken yellow line and the broken line is beside your lane, what does that mean?
options: a:You may pass another vehicle on the left when no oncoming traffic is present.,b:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,c:You are allowed to make only right turns in this area.,d:You must always yield to oncoming traffic before passing.
note: When the broken line is next to your lane, it indicates you are in a passing zone and may pass on the left if it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: On slippery surfaces such as snow or ice, which practice is correct?
options: a:Shift to a low gear before descending steep hills and increase following distance,b:Maintain usual following distance,c:Pump brakes only if you have ABS,d:Tailgate to keep warm
note: On slippery surfaces shift to a low gear for steep descents, increase following distance, and avoid sudden stops; pump brakes only if no ABS.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to warn them,b:Yield the right-of-way to them,c:Ask them to wait until you pass,d:Proceed if they are on the sidewalk
note: You must yield the right-of-way to blind or partially blind pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:In the lane closest to the centerline,b:Near the right-hand side of the road,c:On the left of the centerline,d:In the median
note: Start the left turn from the lane nearest the centerline and turn into the first legal lane of the road you enter.

question: Before changing lanes, what checks should you make?
options: a:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.,b:Check the inside rearview mirror.,c:Slow down.
note: Use mirrors and a shoulder check to verify the lane is clear before changing lanes.

question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic when it is safe and legal to do so.,b:Flash your lights at oncoming traffic to warn them.,c:Use the shoulder.,d:Pass only within an intersection.
note: Passing on two-lane roads requires entering the opposing lane; only pass when you have adequate sight distance and no oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway you should be driving:
options: a:At or near the speed of freeway traffic.,b:At the posted speed limit regardless of traffic.,c:Much slower than the flow of traffic.,d:In neutral so you can coast in.
note: Enter the freeway at a speed close to the traffic flow so you can merge safely.

question: Is alcohol the single greatest factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes?
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only for young drivers,d:Only on weekends
note: Alcohol is a leading cause of fatal crashes because it impairs vision, judgment, and reaction time, even below legal limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a roundabout, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down and yield as required.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Come to a complete stop.
note: Approach roundabouts at a reduced speed, yield to traffic in the circle, and enter when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway, you should:
options: a:Move to the lane on your right.,b:Stay in the center lane.,c:Speed up to match the flow of traffic.,d:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane roads, drive in the right lanes unless passing or turning left; if traffic is flowing around you, move right when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing, when is it appropriate to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror,b:After you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle,c:After one vehicle length,d:When the other driver signals
note: Move back only when you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror and it is safe.

question: Which substances can affect driving ability?
options: a:Tranquilizers and sedatives only,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets only,c:Tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, and some over-the-counter drugs,d:Only illegal drugs
note: Many substances—including prescription tranquilizers, sedatives, illegal drugs, and some over-the-counter cold medicines—can impair driving.

question: While in a vehicle on a highway, possessing an open alcoholic beverage container is:
options: a:Legal if you are a passenger.,b:Illegal to drink from or possess an open container.,c:Allowed if the driver is not drinking.,d:Permitted in the trunk only.
note: It is unlawful for occupants to drink or possess open containers of alcohol in a vehicle on a highway.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.,b:Wait for the owner to return.,c:Call your insurance company when you get home.
note: If you strike parked property, leave your contact information securely attached to the vehicle or property you hit.

question: What is required for safe interstate driving?
options: a:The ability to safely drive at higher speeds,b:Being constantly alert,c:Both being alert and able to drive at increased speeds,d:Using cruise control at all times
note: Safe interstate driving requires being constantly alert and able to handle higher speeds and traffic conditions.

question: In bad weather, what is the appropriate way to steer and brake?
options: a:Steer and brake smoothly and avoid sudden inputs,b:Steer off the road immediately,c:Brake sharply to reduce speed quickly,d:Always use high beams for better visibility
note: In inclement weather, use smooth steering and gentle braking to maintain control and reduce skidding risk.

question: How can you keep track of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.
note: Check your rearview mirror regularly to stay aware of traffic approaching from behind.

question: Yellow centerlines on a roadway separate:
options: a:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,b:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,c:All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.
note: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road; solid yellow lines mean no passing, broken yellow means passing is allowed when safe.

question: Which action helps reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Avoid speeding when roads are wet.,b:Maintain tires with proper air pressure.,c:Drive with badly worn tires to improve grip.,d:Keep on cruise control in heavy rain.
note: Hydroplaning risk rises with speed and with worn or underinflated tires; slowing down on wet roads reduces the risk.

question: If your vehicle's wheels run off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes,b:Turn sharply back onto the pavement immediately,c:Accelerate to regain control,d:Open your door and inspect the tire
note: Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and brake gently; wait until speed is reduced to re-enter the roadway safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection where all corners have stop signs, who should yield the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived before you,b:The driver on your left,c:The driver across from you,d:The largest vehicle
note: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive; if multiple arrive together, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.

question: What is the single most effective thing you can do to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Wear your seat belt.,b:Limit your driving to weekdays.,c:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,d:Increase your horn use.
note: Wearing your seat belt is the most effective measure to reduce the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.

question: When exiting the freeway onto a downhill curved ramp, what should you do?
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.,b:Brake hard once you are in the curve.,c:Maintain freeway speed until the curve ends.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curved ramp downhill to maintain control and avoid skidding.

question: What is the typical purpose of orange-colored traffic signs?
options: a:Warning of work zones,b:Indicating school zones,c:Regulatory instructions,d:Marking recreational areas
note: Orange signs usually warn of highway work zones and alert drivers to road workers or temporary conditions.

question: If you are involved in an accident and someone is injured, you should:
options: a:Move the injured away from the scene immediately.,b:Always leave the injured where they are.,c:Not move the injured unnecessarily; keep them warm and administer first aid.
note: Do not move injured persons unless necessary; untrained handling may worsen injuries. Keep the injured warm and provide first aid until skilled help arrives.

question: Before you drive, you should remove snow, frost, and ice from:
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:All windows.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: You must be able to see clearly through all windows and mirrors; remove snow, ice, and frost before driving.

question: What lane width entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:They are entitled to the same full lane width as other vehicles,b:They must stay in bicycle lanes only,c:They are allowed half a lane width,d:They should share lanes with pedestrians
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane just like other motor vehicles.

question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection indicate?
options: a:Yield to traffic and pedestrians,b:Come to a full stop at the intersection,c:Emergency vehicles have priority,d:Pedestrian crossing ahead
note: A red and white triangular sign is a yield sign — slow and yield the right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians; be ready to stop if necessary.

question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line indicates which side may pass?
options: a:The side next to the broken line may pass.,b:Both sides may pass.,c:The side next to the solid line may pass.
note: When your side has the broken yellow line next to your lane, you are permitted to pass when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A 'No stopping' sign means you may only stop for which reason?
options: a:Long enough to unload packages.,b:To discharge passengers.,c:To avoid conflict with other traffic.
note: A 'No stopping' zone only permits stopping to obey traffic controls, comply with an officer, or to avoid conflict with other traffic.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver on the road, what should you do?
options: a:Challenge them.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Speed up.
note: When dealing with an aggressive driver, avoid confrontation; safely get out of their way to reduce risk.

question: Is it permitted to drive while under the influence of medication that impairs your driving?
options: a:If it is prescribed by a physician.,b:If you don't feel drowsy.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Any substance that impairs your ability to drive safely—prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal—makes driving unsafe and is not permitted.

question: What is the act of turning your head to check blind spots before lane changes called?
options: a:A good driving habit.,b:A bad driving habit.,c:Unnecessary.
note: Looking over your shoulder to check blind spots is a proper and necessary driving habit before lane changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady red traffic light requires you to:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection.,b:Stop at the stop line or crosswalk.,c:Stop at the intersection and remain until it turns green.,d:Either a or b depending on markings.
note: A red signal requires you to stop before entering the intersection and to stop at the marked stop line or, if none, before the crosswalk or intersection.

question: Which statements about work zones are accurate?
options: a:Work zones may be moving or stationary and require caution,b:Work zones are marked with black and white signs only,c:You do not need to slow down in work zones,d:Work zones only occur during daytime
note: Work zones can be stationary or moving, are marked with orange signs, and require you to slow down and pay extra attention.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving on a busy street, what is the correct action?
options: a:Turn on four-way flashers and shift to neutral then stop safely,b:Slam on your brakes immediately,c:Call for a tow while continuing to drive,d:Jump out of the vehicle to stop it
note: If the accelerator sticks, shift to neutral, turn on hazard lights, brake carefully, and move off the road; turn off ignition once safe without locking the steering.

question: The statement 'Driving is a privilege, not a right' is:
options: a:True,b:False
note: Driving is a privilege that carries responsibilities; holding a license requires you to keep yourself and others safe.

question: You are approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light. What should you do?
options: a:Drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Stop and wait for the light to change.,c:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
note: A flashing yellow means proceed with caution after yielding to any hazards or cross traffic.

question: How many alcoholic drinks are required to impair your driving ability?
options: a:One drink can impair your driving.,b:Two drinks only.,c:Three drinks only.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect your driving; even a single drink may impair your abilities.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make room for them when it is safe to do so.,b:Assert your right-of-way by speeding up.,c:Always maintain your current position regardless.
note: When possible and safe, adjust speed or position to allow merging vehicles to enter traffic smoothly.

question: When entering traffic from an alley, driveway, or parking lot, you should:
options: a:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,b:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,c:Expect pedestrians to yield to you.,d:Sound your horn and quickly enter traffic.
note: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk area when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot to yield to pedestrians and traffic.

question: When driving where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Understand traffic signals.,b:Run into the street without looking.,c:Only cross at marked crosswalks.,d:Obey adult supervisors at all times.
note: Children may not recognize hazards and can suddenly run into the road; reduce speed and be prepared to stop.

question: What can cause 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.,b:Frequent rest stops.,c:Too much sleep the night before your trip.
note: 'Highway hypnosis' can occur when you stare straight ahead for long periods and stop actively scanning, causing you to zone out.

question: If you are about to be struck from behind, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Letting go of the steering wheel.,b:Pressing your head into the head restraint.,c:Being ready to apply brakes.
note: If hit from the rear, keep a firm grip on the wheel, press your head against the head restraint, and be prepared to brake.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the safest response?
options: a:Call the police immediately.,b:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,c:Flash your vehicle's lights to let the aggressive driver know he is wrong.
note: Avoid escalating the situation; remain calm and get out of the aggressive driver's path.

question: If you're in an accident, what should you do first?
options: a:Help the injured and call police if needed,b:Leave the scene immediately,c:Ignore and continue driving,d:Only move your vehicle if no one is harmed
note: Stop immediately, move the vehicle if safe, call police and ambulance if necessary, and assist the injured without moving them unnecessarily.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Stop and activate your hazard lights.,d:Quickly swerve into the adjacent lane.
note: Animals near the road may bolt or change direction unexpectedly; slow down and proceed cautiously to reduce the risk of a collision.

question: When backing up a vehicle, what is the recommended technique?
options: a:Look through the rear window while driving in reverse at a low speed.,b:Rely solely on the rearview mirror.,c:Press hard on the gas to finish quickly.
note: Turn your head to see out the rear window and reverse slowly; mirrors alone do not show everything behind you.

question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping on:
options: a:Wet or icy roads.,b:Paved highways.,c:When driving at night.,d:Downhill slopes.
note: Stopping distances grow much longer on wet, icy, or loose surfaces; reduce speed and increase following distance under such conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning onto a multi-lane street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the lane closest to your previous lane.,b:Into the middle lane always.,c:Into any lane; then change immediately.
note: When turning onto a street with several lanes moving in your direction, turn into the lane nearest to your approach lane.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.,b:Wait until the truck or bus turns before you turn.,c:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.
note: Large vehicles need extra space to complete right turns; wait until they have finished before making your turn.

question: Why should you avoid using high beams in fog or mist?
options: a:High beams will reflect back into your eyes,b:Oncoming vehicles cannot see high beams,c:Vehicles behind may follow too closely,d:High beams drain battery faster
note: High beams reflect off fog or mist back into your eyes, reducing visibility; use low beams or fog lights instead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From a center lane marked for turns, which maneuver is permitted?
options: a:You may pass slow-moving traffic.,b:You may make U-turns.,c:You may make left turns.
note: Center lanes marked for left turns are reserved for making left turns, not for passing or through travel.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's ability to drive?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Any medication.,c:A lack of sleep.,d:All of the above
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness from lack of sleep.

question: What does a pair of solid white crosswalk lines indicate about pedestrians?
options: a:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.,b:No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.,c:Pedestrians in crosswalks must be given the right-of-way.
note: Marked crosswalk lines show where pedestrians should cross. You must stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

question: If another vehicle is passing you, how should you behave?
options: a:Brake hard.,b:Maintain a constant speed.,c:Speed up.
note: When being passed you should maintain a steady speed and not increase speed so the other driver can safely merge back into the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a steady red traffic light, what must drivers do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop (and may turn right unless prohibited).,b:Drive through if no crossing traffic is present.,c:Stop only if a police officer is present.
note: A steady red light requires a full stop; right turns on red are allowed unless a sign forbids it.

question: How can you avoid remaining in the blind spot of a truck or bus?
options: a:Avoid driving alongside them or tailgating.,b:Flash your headlights at them to alert the driver.,c:Never pass them.
note: Large trucks and buses have significant blind spots to the sides and rear; avoid driving alongside them and do not follow too closely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what conditions may you safely pass on a two-way, two-lane street?
options: a:When you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic and see clearly ahead.,b:Whenever the car ahead is turning left.,c:If your vehicle can reach the necessary passing speed.
note: You may only pass on a two-way, two-lane road if you can see clearly ahead and can return to your lane before oncoming traffic.

question: When must vehicles remain stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing?
options: a:Until the stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.,b:Only until all students are off the bus.,c:Until the bus driver waves you through.
note: Do not proceed until the bus turns off its lights, withdraws the stop arm, and starts moving again.

question: Who is required to wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle in Rhode Island?
options: a:Only the driver,b:Only adult passengers,c:All occupants including driver and passengers
note: Rhode Island law requires drivers and passengers of all ages to be properly restrained by seat belts; some children require additional child restraints.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving too slowly is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,c:The speed you drive has no impact on safety.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can create hazards and increase the likelihood of crashes.

question: What is the best way to handle being tailgated?
options: a:Slam on brakes to make them back off.,b:Speed up to create distance.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.,d:Brake-check them.
note: If someone is following too closely, let them pass or safely move over; avoid aggressive responses.

question: For drivers age 21 and older, it is illegal to operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of at least:
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.02 percent.,d:0.10 percent.
note: Drivers 21 or older are prohibited from operating a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher; driving under the influence is both illegal and dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If there is no marked crosswalk at a stop sign, where must you stop?
options: a:True,b:False
note: At a stop sign you must stop at the stop line, if present; if not, stop before entering the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what is the safest thing to do?
options: a:Go to the next exit.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
note: Do not stop, back up, or make illegal turns on the freeway; proceed to the next exit and re-route.

question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:After completing the lane change,b:Just before changing lanes,c:Early enough so other drivers know your intent,d:Only if the other driver signals
note: Signal early enough before passing so other drivers have clear notice of your intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes you must:
options: a:Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.,b:Signal only if there is visible traffic.,c:Signal only when driving at night.
note: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or leaving a curb; do not form the habit of failing to signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting a highway, when should you reduce your speed?
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane.,b:On the main road just before the exit lane.,c:Only when you reach the toll booth.,d:While still on the through lanes.
note: Do not slow down on the mainline; enter the exit lane and then reduce your speed on the deceleration ramp.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it unsafe or illegal to make a U-turn?
options: a:Near the top of a hill or in the middle of a curve.,b:Anywhere that you can do a 180-degree turn safely.,c:On a freeway always.
note: U-turns near hilltops or in the middle of curves are unsafe because you cannot see oncoming traffic.

question: When a school bus is loading or unloading children, what must motorists do?
options: a:Stop regardless of your direction of travel.,b:Only stop if traveling in the same direction.,c:Slow down and be ready to stop.
note: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children with red lights flashing, motorists must stop in all directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: It is illegal to follow within what distance of an emergency vehicle responding to an emergency?
options: a:1,000 feet,b:500 feet,c:750 feet
note: You must leave space behind emergency vehicles responding with lights or siren; it is unlawful to follow within 500 feet.

question: Is it unlawful for a car to share a lane with a motorcycle?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane; a car should not try to share a lane with a motorcycle.

question: What does a 'No passing zone' sign indicate?
options: a:To speed up slightly.,b:That it is not safe to pass.,c:To maintain a steady speed.
note: A 'No passing zone' sign means passing is not legal or safe in the indicated area due to limited visibility or other hazards.

question: If poor weather reduces your visibility, what should you do regarding following distance?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
note: When visibility is reduced by weather, increase following distance to allow more reaction time.

question: When may you legally cross a solid yellow centerline?
options: a:Only to make a turn into or out of a private driveway or to follow traffic laws allowing turns.,b:During daylight hours.,c:At any time when no oncoming traffic is present.,d:To pass slower traffic moving in the same direction.
note: Solid yellow centerlines generally prohibit passing but may be crossed to make a permitted left turn or enter a driveway when safe.

question: If the driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger, what should you do?
options: a:Avoid following the driver's example.,b:Know the driver is reducing their safety margin.,c:Give the vehicle extra space.
note: If a nearby driver appears distracted, increase the gap around them because their risk of causing a crash is higher.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light means:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if there is no traffic.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light instructs drivers to slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection.

question: If a traffic light shows both a red light and a green arrow, can you turn in the arrow's direction?
options: a:True — you may turn in the direction of the green arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians,b:False — you must wait until the red light changes,c:Only if no pedestrians are present,d:Only if a police officer signals you
note: A green arrow permits the indicated movement even if another signal is red, provided you yield to any traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a traffic signal showing a green arrow and a red light mean?
options: a:You may travel only in the direction of the green arrow.,b:You may only drive straight ahead.,c:You must wait for a solid green light to go any direction.
note: A green arrow permits movement only in the arrow's direction and only if the way is clear.

question: To ensure your physical condition does not make driving unsafe, you should:
options: a:Drive within your physical limitations.,b:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.,c:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.,d:All of the above.
note: Maintain good health, understand how medications affect you, and drive only within your abilities to remain safe.

question: What does an orange-colored road sign generally warn of?
options: a:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.,b:A school zone is ahead.,c:A railroad crossing is ahead.
note: Orange signs indicate construction or maintenance work zones; exercise extra caution.

question: What is alcohol classified as in terms of drug category?
options: a:A depressant,b:A stimulant,c:An antihistamine,d:A hallucinogen
note: Alcohol is a depressant that impairs judgment and slows reflexes, increasing crash risk.

question: Why is driving at night generally more dangerous than daytime driving?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road is always slipperier at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night irrespective of visibility.
note: Reduced visibility and glare from headlights limit how far you can see at night, increasing risk.

question: Which practice is unsafe on the interstate?
options: a:Changing lanes without signaling,b:Slower traffic keeping to the right,c:Proceeding to the next exit if you miss yours,d:Using turn signals before lane changes
note: Failing to signal is unsafe; always signal when changing lanes. Slower traffic should keep right and if you miss an exit, go to the next one.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed if clear.,b:Come to a complete stop, check for traffic, and go when safe.,c:Ignore it unless you see other cars.,d:Yield only to vehicles on the left.
note: A flashing red light is treated as a stop sign: stop completely, yield to others, and proceed when safe.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.,b:A driver must stop and then proceed when the way is clear.,c:A driver must stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.
note: A red arrow requires drivers to stop and remain stopped until a green signal or arrow permits movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To make a left turn from a multi-lane, one-way street, you should begin from:
options: a:The left lane.,b:The center of the roadway.,c:The right lane.,d:The shoulder.
note: On one-way streets, start left turns from the leftmost lane and complete the turn into the leftmost lane of the street you enter.

question: What is the correct technique for backing a vehicle?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing slowly.,b:Rely only on mirrors while backing.,c:Open your door to see whether it is safe to reverse.
note: When backing, look directly through the rear window and proceed slowly; don't rely solely on mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When stopped at an intersection with a stop sign, which visual check should you make?
options: a:Look right first, then left, then right again.,b:Check your rearview mirror for tailgaters only.,c:Move when the car ahead moves without further checks.
note: At a stop, look right then left then right again to ensure no hidden approaching vehicles.

question: What should you be prepared for when passing a row of parked cars?
options: a:A person or vehicle unexpectedly entering your lane.,b:All others will respect your right-of-way.,c:Drive close to the parked cars to allow traffic to pass.
note: People or vehicles can suddenly step out from between parked cars; leave space and be ready to react.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how far should you stay behind?
options: a:Farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle.,b:Closer than you would a passenger vehicle.,c:Directly to its right to prepare to pass.
note: Because trucks have large blind spots and longer stopping distances, leave extra following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
options: a:20 feet,b:30 feet,c:40 feet
note: Drivers may not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection to avoid blocking visibility.

question: If you are following a school bus or a tank truck that carries hazardous liquids, what should you be prepared to do at railroad crossings?
options: a:Pass them on the right.,b:Decrease your following distance.,c:Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.
note: School buses and tank trucks carrying flammable liquids are required to stop at railroad crossings; follow and be prepared to stop as well.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn you should:
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Sound your horn continuously.,c:Turn your front wheels left early.,d:Drive partway into the crosswalk.
note: Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when making left turns; keep wheels straight until you begin the turn.

question: When confronted with an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, what should you do?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder.,b:Try to split the difference between them.,c:Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.
note: Avoid dealing with two hazards at once. Let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the bicyclist when it is safe to do so.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,b:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is especially important.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
note: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter requires extra caution and vehicle checks.

question: Is a railroad crossbuck treated like a yield sign?
options: a:True — you must yield at a crossbuck,b:False — treat it like a stop sign,c:Only if bells are sounding,d:Only if gates are present
note: A railroad crossbuck indicates you must yield the right-of-way to approaching trains and railroad equipment.

question: A solid white centerline on a multi-lane road means:
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and lane changes are discouraged.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed.,c:Center turn lane ahead.,d:Parking allowed on either side.
note: Solid white lines separate lanes going the same direction and indicate lane changes are discouraged or prohibited.

question: If you become tired while driving, what is the safest action?
options: a:Stop and rest or change drivers,b:Drink caffeine and keep driving,c:Open the window and continue,d:Turn up the radio and drive on
note: If tired, stop and rest or switch drivers; do not rely on short-term fixes like caffeine to safely continue driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, which actions should you perform?
options: a:Check your side and rearview mirrors.,b:Give a turn signal to signal your intentions.,c:Check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.,d:All of the above
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, and verify other drivers are not also moving into that lane.

question: Does a 'Merging lanes' sign indicate drivers should prepare to change lanes or allow others to merge?
options: a:True — be prepared to change lanes or allow merging,b:False — it means reduce speed only,c:False — it means stop and wait,d:True — but only on highways
note: A 'Merging lanes' sign warns that two lanes will become one and drivers should be ready to change lanes or allow merging traffic.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Try to pull up the pedal with your hand.,b:Shift to neutral and apply steady braking.,c:Shift to park while moving.,d:Turn off your headlights.
note: Keep control, shift to neutral, apply steady brakes, steer safely off the road, and then turn off the engine.

question: When planning to pass another vehicle, what should you assume about the other driver?
options: a:Do not assume they will make space for you to return,b:Assume they will let you pass if you signal,c:Assume they will maintain a constant speed,d:Assume they will speed up to help you pass
note: Never assume the other driver will yield space; confirm it is safe before you pass and return to your lane.
