question: On a vertically arranged traffic signal, what is the top-to-bottom order of the lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Green, red, yellow.
note: On vertical signals red is always at the top, then yellow, then green at the bottom.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrives first.,b:The driver who arrives last.,c:The driver to the left if two stop simultaneously.,d:The driver who signals first.
note: At a four-way stop, the vehicle that arrives first has the right-of-way; if two arrive together, the vehicle on the right goes first.

question: If a traffic light changes to a steady yellow before you enter the intersection, you should:
options: a:Increase speed to get through.,b:Come to a safe stop if you have not entered, c:Drive normally.,d:Back up to avoid being trapped.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will soon be red; if you have not entered the intersection, you should safely stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,b:Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb rather than traffic if the brakes fail.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, you become:
options: a:More sober.,b:More intoxicated.,c:More coordinated.,d:Less affected at first.
note: Higher BAC corresponds with greater impairment and increased risk while driving.

question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:So other road users know your intentions.,b:Because it's illegal to turn off a signal before the turn is finished.,c:Because turning off a signal is always unsafe.
note: Signaling communicates your intentions to drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians and helps prevent collisions.

question: Regulatory signs are typically what color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:White.,b:Green.,c:Blue.,d:Yellow.
note: Regulatory signs are usually white with black markings and indicate legal requirements such as speed limits and turn restrictions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it safe to attempt to pass more than one vehicle at a time?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Never try to pass more than one vehicle at a time; passing multiple vehicles increases risk and reduces escape options.

question: To check blind spots for lane changes, drivers should look:
options: a:Only the left outside mirror.,b:Over their left or right shoulder.,c:Only the inside rearview mirror.
note: Look over the appropriate shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes; mirrors alone do not show everything.

question: A single dashed yellow centerline means:
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: A single dashed yellow line separates opposite-direction traffic and indicates that passing is permitted when safe.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, you should:
options: a:Pull over to the right and stop.,b:Stop where you are without moving to the side.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.,d:Continue slowly and let the emergency vehicle pass.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with sirens or lights, safely pull to the right and stop to allow it to pass.

question: When is the pavement most hazardous for turning and stopping during rainy weather?
options: a:During the first half hour of rain.,b:After it has been raining all day.,c:One half hour after the rain stops.
note: The first half hour of rain mixes oil and water on the pavement, making it especially slippery for turns and stops.

question: When is it prohibited to cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When doing so would interfere with other traffic.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:When the car ahead of you is disabled.,d:Never — you may cross a broken line anytime.
note: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes as long as it can be done safely and without interfering with traffic flow.

question: If you parallel park facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.,b:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.,c:Keep your wheels straight.
note: When parked downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the vehicle will roll toward the curb if brakes fail.

question: Which of these does NOT help promote safe night driving?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean.,b:Use interior dome light while driving to read directions.,c:Be mindful that tinted windows reduce night visibility.,d:Carry a flashlight for emergencies.
note: Using interior lights while driving can cause glare and reduce your ability to see outside; keep interior lighting low while driving at night.

question: Collisions are more likely to occur when vehicles in traffic are:
options: a:Traveling at different speeds than the flow of traffic.,b:All traveling at about the same speed.,c:Traveling slower than the posted limit.
note: When one vehicle travels much faster or slower than surrounding traffic, collision risk increases.

question: Why is a leaking exhaust system hazardous?
options: a:It can allow carbon monoxide to enter the vehicle and cause poisoning.,b:It causes a loss of hearing.,c:It increases fuel efficiency.,d:It causes air pollution.
note: A leaking exhaust can let carbon monoxide into the passenger compartment; defective exhaust parts should be repaired immediately to prevent poisoning.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:Lower your ability to concentrate on driving.,b:Decrease chances of an accident.,c:Cause you to fall asleep at the wheel.,d:Improve reaction time.
note: Strong emotions and stress can reduce concentration and decision-making, increasing crash risk.

question: In bad weather, what should you do about following distance?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Decrease your following distance.,c:Increase your speed to reach your destination faster.
note: On wet or slippery roads increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react and stop.

question: What is the only medically proven way to remove alcohol and drug combinations from your system?
options: a:Drinking coffee.,b:Allowing your body time.,c:Taking a cold shower.,d:Exercising vigorously.
note: Metabolism over time is the only way to lower BAC and eliminate most drugs from the body; other measures do not work.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror,b:After about three seconds,c:When you are one vehicle length ahead,d:When the passed vehicle signals you back
note: Return to the lane only when you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and it's safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:The posted maximum speed only.,b:A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent for conditions.,c:The average speed of traffic.,d:Any speed below the legal limit.
note: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for road, weather, traffic, and visibility conditions, even if below the posted limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the centerline shows a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line with the broken line on your side, when may you pass?
options: a:If traffic is clear and it is safe to do so,b:Only when you are on an expressway,c:Only in an emergency,d:Never
note: If the broken line is on your side, you may pass when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear its siren, you must:
options: a:Slow down and continue in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane at the same speed.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop.,d:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: Immediately pull to the right side of the road and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers,b:Human error,c:Bad weather
note: Most crashes occur because of human error—drivers not seeing others or acting unpredictably.

question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Type of alcoholic beverage consumed.,b:Your body weight.,c:How much you drink.,d:How much time passes between drinks.
note: BAC is influenced by how much alcohol you drink, your weight, and how quickly you drink; the type of drink (beer vs wine) does not change the alcohol content once consumed.

question: Which of these is a safe driving habit?
options: a:Checking rearview mirrors frequently.,b:Staring fixedly at the road ahead.,c:Using high beams in fog.,d:Driving with the parking brake on.
note: To remain aware of hazards, check your mirrors every 2–5 seconds and scan the road rather than staring straight ahead.

question: What should a driver taking a non-prescription drug do?
options: a:Read the drug labels before driving,b:Mix it with alcohol to feel normal,c:Assume it won't affect driving if it's over-the-counter,d:Ignore all warning labels
note: Many over-the-counter drugs can impair driving; read labels and consult a doctor or pharmacist if unsure.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.,b:Drive slowly and expect others to move out of your way.,c:Honk your horn to warn approaching traffic.
note: Stop before entering the roadway from a driveway and yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is a situation when you must not attempt to pass another vehicle?
options: a:On a hill or curve.,b:When school bus lights are flashing.,c:When approaching an intersection.
note: You should never pass where visibility is restricted (such as on a hill or curve), at intersections, on railroad crossings, or where signs prohibit passing. (Also, do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided roadway.)

question: Is holding a driver license a right or a privilege?
options: a:It is a privilege, not a right,b:It is an absolute right,c:It is neither,d:It is a constitutional guarantee
note: Driving is a privilege granted by the state and must be earned and maintained, not an inherent right.

question: If you are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle with siren and lights is approaching, you should:
options: a:Stop immediately in the intersection.,b:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,c:Panic and brake hard.,d:Pull to the left and stop.
note: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in the intersection, clear the intersection, then pull to the curb or right edge and stop to yield the right-of-way.

question: What should you do when you encounter a flashing yellow light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution; you do not need to come to a complete stop.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:Children lack adult reflexes and are smaller/harder to see,b:They are always required to stay out of the road,c:They always follow traffic rules,d:They can stop quickly if needed
note: Children are less predictable and harder to see; give them extra space near schools, parks, and neighborhoods.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do with your vehicle lights?
options: a:Turn on your headlights (low beam).,b:Use parking lights.,c:Use four-way flashers at all times.
note: At dusk or on overcast days you must use headlights; dim to low beams near other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street, what should you do?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.,b:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles using lights and sirens by pulling to the right edge of the roadway and stopping until they pass. If you are in an intersection, clear it first then stop.

question: When you spot a school crossing sign, how should you respond?
options: a:Always stop, whether there’s a stop sign or not.,b:Always sound your horn when you see children.,c:Watch for children and be ready to stop.
note: Pentagonal signs indicate you are approaching a school zone or crossing. Be alert for children and be ready to stop.

question: What headlight setting should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your low beam headlights.,c:Use your high beams.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if the light is green but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,b:Proceed into the intersection and wait.,c:Turn left to find another route immediately.
note: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot clear it; you can be ticketed for blocking the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal, you should:
options: a:Speed up to pass before they cross.,b:Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.,c:Honk to warn them to hurry.,d:Drive around them.
note: Yield to pedestrians even if they are crossing against the signal; stop if necessary to avoid a collision.

question: To reduce headlight glare at night, where should you look?
options: a:Briefly toward the right side of the road,b:Stare straight at the headlights,c:Look at the centerline only,d:Flash your high beams back
note: Glance briefly to the right side of the road to avoid glare and then resume checking the road ahead.

question: Which driving behavior can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Slowing down gradually instead of braking hard.,b:Accelerating quickly whenever possible.,c:Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.
note: Anticipating traffic and slowing gradually reduces unnecessary acceleration and improves fuel economy.

question: If you discover a vehicle defect that could affect safe operation, when should it be corrected?
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,b:Correct the defect when you can afford it.,c:Drive the vehicle at slower speeds until you can fix it.
note: Any defect that affects safe operation should be corrected promptly and before driving when possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure to change lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, look over your shoulder for blind spots, then change lanes,b:Signal then immediately change lanes without checking mirrors,c:Check mirror and change lanes without signaling,d:Only signal if other traffic is present
note: Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and the target lane, and change lanes when safe.

question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and maintenance areas?
options: a:Orange.,b:Red.,c:Yellow.
note: Orange signs, cones, and barriers indicate construction or maintenance work zones; use extra caution.

question: Lanes of traffic traveling in the same direction are divided by what color lines?
options: a:White,b:Yellow,c:Red
note: Solid white lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction; broken white lines mean you may change lanes when safe.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Drivers next to the broken line may pass when safe.,b:Passing is permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is prohibited for both directions.,d:The solid line side may pass.
note: Where a broken yellow line is adjacent to a solid yellow line, only traffic next to the broken line may pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn.,b:Get off at the next exit and return safely.,c:Back up on the shoulder.,d:Signal and reverse into the exit.
note: Do not stop or back up on a highway; continue to the next exit and re-route safely.

question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.,b:Maintain your current speed and steer straight.,c:Brake hard immediately.
note: Hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas, and do not brake hard until you have control; then pull off safely.

question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.,b:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,c:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.
note: When parked on an incline, turn your wheels so the vehicle will roll away from traffic and toward the curb or road edge if the brakes fail.

question: Which driving technique helps prevent crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Engage the four-wheel drive on their vehicles.,b:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.,c:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.
note: Slowing down and increasing your following distance are the most effective ways to reduce crash risk on slippery roads.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction from water on the road, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent your vehicle from sliding.,b:Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.,c:Slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.
note: If you start to hydroplane, gradually reduce speed by releasing the accelerator and avoid braking until traction is regained.

question: Which is a consequence of worn or bald tires?
options: a:Increased stopping distance.,b:Improved fuel efficiency.,c:Better traction in rain.,d:Reduced risk of hydroplaning.
note: Worn tires reduce traction, increase stopping distance, impair turning ability, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

question: As vehicle speed increases, what should you do regarding observation?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Look well ahead of your vehicle.,c:Change lanes frequently.
note: Stopping distance and time to react increase with speed; look farther ahead to spot hazards and allow time to respond.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings and road signs?
options: a:They provide information and guidance for drivers,b:They are generally decorative,c:They apply only in construction zones,d:They are optional suggestions
note: Road markings and signs guide positioning, passing zones, warnings, and other driving information essential for safety.

question: How can sudden wind gusts on highways affect vehicles?
options: a:They generally affect only the movement of large vehicles.,b:They only cause visibility problems.,c:They can cause problems for all vehicles.
note: Strong wind can affect all vehicles, reducing visibility and sometimes physically moving a vehicle, though large vehicles may be more affected.

question: Compared to smaller cars, larger vehicles generally have:
options: a:No blind spots.,b:Smaller blind spots.,c:Larger blind spots.
note: The larger the vehicle, the larger the blind spots; trucks and large SUVs may have areas they cannot see in their mirrors.

question: When parallel parking, how close should your wheels be to the curb?
options: a:Within 18 inches of the curb,b:Within 12 inches of the curb,c:Within 10 inches of the curb,d:Against the curb
note: When parallel parking, park with your wheels parallel to and within 12 inches of the curb so your vehicle is visible and not disruptive to traffic.

question: When bright headlights from an approaching car affect your vision at night, what should you do?
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Stop until the other driver passes.,c:Look directly into the headlights to adjust.
note: Look toward the right edge of your lane and use peripheral vision to follow the vehicle until it passes.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which direction should a pedestrian walk?
options: a:Facing oncoming traffic (on the side of the road facing traffic).,b:In the same direction as vehicle traffic.,c:On the side with the lightest traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk facing oncoming vehicles so they can see and react to traffic.

question: When driving in traffic, the safest approach is to:
options: a:Drive faster than the flow of traffic.,b:Fluctuate your speed to stay alert.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted speed limits.
note: Crashes often occur when drivers travel much faster or slower than surrounding traffic; drive with the flow at legal speeds.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, check traffic, and gradually steer back onto the roadway when safe.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Stop and wait for assistance.
note: Reduce speed, scan for traffic, and carefully re-enter the roadway when it is safe.

question: Which of these statements about railroad crossings is correct?
options: a:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal.,b:You have the right-of-way and do not need to stop.,c:You should use cruise control when going over railroad tracks.,d:Always come to a full stop at every railroad crossing.
note: Drivers must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Use caution near tracks.

question: True or false: You should use high beam headlights while driving in fog.
options: a:True.,b:False.
note: High beams can reflect off fog and reduce visibility; use low beams in foggy conditions.

question: When making a left turn, must you yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction?
options: a:True,b:False
note: When turning left, yield to oncoming bicycles just as you would to oncoming motor vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive more slowly than the flow of traffic under normal conditions, you will most likely:
options: a:Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,b:Improve traffic flow.,c:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving significantly below the normal speed of traffic can impede movement and may result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statements about driving speed are true?
options: a:As speed increases the chance of fatality increases,b:As speed increases you should increase following distance,c:Both A and B are true,d:Neither A nor B is true
note: Higher speeds increase the chance of severe injury or death; increase following distance as speed increases.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed through if clear.,b:Come to a full stop, then go when it is safe.,c:Wait until the light turns green.,d:Stop only if other traffic is present.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: stop completely, yield to others, and proceed when safe.

question: How can you relieve fatigue on a long trip?
options: a:Stop and rest every two hours,b:Drive with windows open the whole time,c:Keep driving until you reach your destination,d:Take a single long break every six hours
note: Stop every two hours for a short break or switch drivers; if drowsy, find a safe place to nap or spend the night.

question: Which substances may lead to arrest for DUII or impair driving?
options: a:Beer, wine, and other liquor,b:Illegal drugs and some prescription medicines,c:Inhalants like glue or paint,d:All of the above
note: Alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications can impair driving and result in DUII charges.

question: When driving at night, which practice is recommended?
options: a:Always use high beams.,b:Look directly at oncoming headlights.,c:Increase your following distance.,d:Drive at the posted speed regardless of visibility.
note: Increase your following distance at night and use proper headlight settings to maintain safe stopping distances.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Apply the brakes hard immediately.
note: If a vehicle skids, avoid braking; steer gently to regain control until stable.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on a highway, you should:
options: a:Stop in the travel lane.,b:Park with all four wheels off the traveled portion of the road if possible.,c:Leave the vehicle in the middle of the road.,d:Continue driving slowly to the next exit.
note: If possible, move your vehicle completely off the main traveled portion of the roadway and turn on hazard lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you avoid collisions caused by vehicles in your blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.,b:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,c:Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots; do not rely solely on mirrors.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you begin driving.,b:Whenever you happen to need them while moving.,c:After you get into the car but before fastening your belt.,d:After the vehicle is moving.
note: Adjust mirrors, seat, and seat belt before you move the vehicle to ensure maximum visibility and safety.

question: Combining alcohol with drugs typically causes:
options: a:Decreased effects of both.,b:Increased and unpredictable effects of both.,c:A cure for dizziness.,d:No change.
note: Alcohol combined with other drugs can amplify effects and greatly increase impairment and risk.

question: At what speeds may a car begin to hydroplane on wet roads?
options: a:At speeds around 35 miles per hour or higher,b:Only above 55 miles per hour,c:Below 25 miles per hour,d:Hydroplaning does not depend on speed
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds near 35 mph when tires cannot channel water away, causing loss of road contact.

question: What is the effect of excessive speed?
options: a:It increases the likelihood of serious injury and death,b:It consistently helps you avoid obstacles,c:It saves significant time on trips,d:It improves fuel efficiency
note: Excessive speed increases crash severity and the likelihood of fatal or serious injuries; it rarely saves meaningful time.

question: If a HAWK (High Intensity Activated Crosswalk) signal goes dark (black), drivers should:
options: a:Come to a full stop.,b:Proceed past the crosswalk with caution.,c:Always yield to pedestrians without slowing.,d:Speed up to clear the crosswalk.
note: When the HAWK signal is dark, drivers should proceed with caution past the crosswalk; the dark signal indicates no pedestrian activation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about stopping in a travel lane is correct?
options: a:You should not stop in a travel lane for any reason.,b:You may stop to drop off passengers in a travel lane.,c:You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong freeway ramp.
note: Do not stop in a travel lane; if you miss a turn or exit, continue to a safe place to turn around rather than backing up.

question: Your blind spot is the area of the road that:
options: a:You see in your rearview mirror.,b:Directly behind your vehicle.,c:You cannot see without moving your head.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors and require a head check to see before changing lanes.

question: In a minor intersection collision with no injuries, what should you do with your vehicle?
options: a:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so,b:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive,c:Always remain in the vehicle and wait for an officer,d:Immediately drive away to avoid congestion
note: If there are no injuries and it's safe, move vehicles out of the traffic lane to reduce hazard and exchange information.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, you should:
options: a:Check your side view mirror.,b:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles.,c:Check your rearview mirror.,d:Signal without checking mirrors.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then glance over your shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear.

question: Do emotions affect driving performance?
options: a:True — strong emotions can impair perception and decision-making,b:False — emotions do not affect driving,c:Only extreme emotions have any effect,d:Emotions only matter for new drivers
note: Strong emotions like anger or fear can alter how you perceive and respond to situations and often negatively affect driving.

question: What is the only thing that reduces blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drinking coffee or caffeine,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:The passage of time,d:Cold showers
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and remove alcohol; nothing else reliably speeds sobriety.

question: When is it allowed to park or stop on a freeway shoulder?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:Any time if you turn on hazard flashers.,c:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
note: Parking or stopping on a freeway shoulder is prohibited except in emergencies.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the best practice?
options: a:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of traffic and merge safely.,b:Proceed very slowly and wait for a gap.,c:Turn on hazard lights while merging.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait.
note: Use the acceleration lane to get up to freeway speed so you can merge smoothly with existing traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When you are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.,b:When you are on a hill or curve.,c:When there is a solid line next to your lane.
note: A broken line next to your lane indicates passing is permitted when it is safe to do so; do not pass on curves or hills where you cannot see ahead.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction area, what must you do?
options: a:Follow the flagger's directions,b:Ignore and follow surrounding traffic instead,c:Assume the flagger is not authorized,d:Proceed only if other drivers do
note: Obey flaggers in construction zones; failure to comply is illegal and endangers workers and motorists.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate, after matching the speed of traffic and signaling, you should:
options: a:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed since you have the right-of-way.,b:Merge carefully into the gap.,c:Wait for the lane to clear before merging.
note: Identify a gap, accelerate to match traffic, signal, and merge into the gap when it is safe; do not assume others will yield.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving.,b:Excessive speed for conditions.,c:Following too closely.,d:All of the above.
note: Distracted driving, driving too fast for conditions, and tailgating are all major contributors to crashes.

question: Approaching railroad tracks, you should:
options: a:Speed up to beat any approaching train.,b:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,c:Drive around lowered gates if no train is visible.,d:Ignore crossing signs at night.
note: Always look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop when approaching a crossing.

question: Which types of drugs can impair your driving?
options: a:Illegal drugs, prescription medications, and some over-the-counter remedies.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only prescription drugs.,d:Only cold medicines.
note: Many substances — illegal drugs, prescription medicines, and certain OTC products — can impair driving ability and reaction time.

question: If your tire suddenly blows out while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.,c:Keep driving normally.
note: Do not apply the brakes immediately. Grip the wheel, stay in your lane, reduce speed gradually, and pull off the road when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic to merge safely?
options: a:Use side mirror and look over your shoulder as well as mirrors.,b:Use only your rearview mirror.,c:Use rearview and side mirrors but not a shoulder check.
note: When merging, use mirrors and look over your shoulder to check blind spots and freeway traffic.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Apply your parking brake.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: First ease off the accelerator; if more slowing is needed, apply the brakes gently and steadily.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a fire engine follows you but is not using lights or siren, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to drive normally.,b:Stop immediately.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: If an emergency vehicle is following without lights or sirens, you do not need to clear the way; continue normally.

question: Alcohol in any concentration acts as:
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:An enhancer of alertness.,d:An anesthetic.
note: Alcohol depresses the central nervous system, slowing reflexes, reaction time, and judgment.
